“Of course, I want to finish as high as possible. I want win as many races as possible, but what’s more important to me is to finish the season on a positive momentum rather than necessarily that final order.

“If I finish second, third, fourth, fifth, I will [only] lose sleep or gain sleep based on the performances as opposed to that. As long as it’s not P1, in this sport, it’s kind of that or nothing really.”

Sports.title: Perez performs Cadillac show run in Mexico City – in a car from F1: The Movie | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Sergio Perez performed a show run in his home country ahead of this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

The Cadillac driver took to the streets of Mexico City along the Paseo de la Reforma. Over 100,000 fans were estimated to have attended the event.

The event promoters billed this as Perez’s fourth appearance in a Formula 1 car on the streets of his home country. However it appears Perez was not in fact driving a real F1 car.

Teams ordinarily use older cars to conduct show runs and ‘Testing of Previous Cars’. As this is Cadillac’s first season in F1 they have no such cars available.

The team therefore used one of the cars used to film “F1: The Movie”. These cars were based on Formula 2 chassis – the filmmakers purchased six for this purpose – and used bodywork modified by the Mercedes F1 team.

Cadillac yesterday confirmed Perez will continue to drive for them until at least 2029. He will make his 300th start in his home race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez this weekend.

“Being able to celebrate my 300th grand prix here is extraordinary,” said Perez. “A lot had to happen for this to become a reality, and being able to share this moment with everyone who has supported me, in such an iconic place as Reforma, makes it incredibly special to me. Thank you to Cadillac and everyone who made this possible.”

Sports.title: Fans “pay a bit less attention” to Formula 1 as calendar gets longer – Sainz | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr suspects the growing size of the Formula 1 calendar may not be helping to make the sport more popular.

F1 has increased the number of rounds to 24, though only 23 are scheduled to happen this year due to the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. The number could fall further if either of the final two rounds are cancelled.

If the final rounds go ahead as planned, F1 will hold nine events in just eleven weeks. Sainz says he would have enjoyed more regular races when he was younger but suspects it may have become a turn-off for some fans.

“I think if I were a fan, I would love it because the more F1 I can watch on TV, the better,” he said. “I remember when I was a kid and there were only 16 races in the calendar, or 18. I used to miss Formula 1 [because it was not on] for a lot of weekends.

“But we also need to consider as a sport if that’s something that maybe is also counterproductive. Sometimes you need to miss the sport to get people engaged. When you get so many races in a row, people or the sport can maybe feel a bit like a league, like the Premier League rather than the Champions League. So maybe you pay a bit less attention to the matches or to the races in this case.

“So, it’s more a philosophy for the sport to consider whether you want to keep having so many races in a row.”

However Sainz, a director of the Grand Prix Drivers’ Association, is also concerned about the effect F1’s long calendar has on the teams’ staff.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“More important than that, I think as the GPDA, we’ve been told more or less that 24 races, 25 races is the limit of the championship that they’re willing to go for. I don’t know if that will be the case, the more offers there are to keep increasing venues. But I think that is the limit.

“I think it’s more about the members of the team that are going to spend only three or four days at home, or five days at home every month. And it’s the people in the teams that get the tougher end rather than the drivers. I think we are in a more privileged position in that sense.

“So, let’s see. I have the motivation to do however many races we need to do. I have the will to race. I love racing. But it is true that this end of the triple header, with three triple headers in a row, is going to be tough for the body, tough for the people, tough for the mind.”

Sports.title: F1 newcomers Tsolov, Mini and Slater among nine drivers to run in practice on Friday | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Nine teams will give practice outings to inexperienced drivers at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

Three of them – Red Bull junior driver Nikola Tsolov, Alpine’s Gabriele Mini and Audi’s Freddie Slater – will make their debuts in an official F1 test session. Tsolov will drive for Red Bull’s second F1 team, Racing Bulls.

Teams must give four opportunities to inexperienced drivers – two in each of their cars – in first practice sessions over the course of the year.

Among the others driving this weekend is Luke Browning. Williams has entered him for a fifth session this year after he completed no laps when he appeared for them at the Circuit de Catalunya. Colton Herta will also appear in a session for the fifth time this year at Cadillac.

Also in action this weekend are Leonardo Fornaroli and Jak Crawford, making their fourth appearances for McLaren and Aston Martin respectively. McLaren recently confirmed Fornaroli, the 2025 Formula 2 champion, will drive for its new WEC Hypercar team.

Ayumu Iwasa will also make his fourth appearance this year, and third for Red Bull. He has also previously driven for Racing Bulls. Ryo Hirakawa will appear for the third time in a Haas this season.

More than half the teams will have completed their obligation to run drivers on four occasions after next week’s Brazilian Grand Prix. Unlike in previous years, none of the remaining rounds are sprint events, meaning they theoretically have more opportunities to run their junior drivers. But with doubt continuing to hang over whether the final races in the Middle East will go ahead, teams appear to be ensuring they do not fail to fulfil their practice quotas should they be cancelled.

Sports.title: New contract to keep Perez racing for Cadillac until at least 2029 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Cadillac has announced a new contract with Sergio Perez, days before he starts his 300th grand prix at home in Mexico.

Perez will remain at the team until at least 2029 under his new, long-term deal.

He joined the F1 newcomers last year ahead of their debut this season.

“Building a competitive team in F1 is a long-term journey, and securing Checo’s talent and leadership gives us the continuity and commitment we need to build on the strong foundation established in our first year,” said CEO Dan Towriss. “Together, we are focused on the next phase of our journey, pushing the team forward and making progress up the grid.”

Cadillac is yet to confirm the identity of Perez’s team mate for next year. The team are yet to score a point, Perez having achieved a best finish of 14th, current team mate Valtteri Bottas 13th.

“Building a Formula 1 team from the ground up takes time, relentless work and patience, but the progress we are making together is incredibly rewarding,” said Perez. “There is still a lot of work ahead of us and I am fully committed for the next three years.”

Perez has experienced disappointment with multi-year contracts before. In 2019 he agreed a three-year deal to stay at Lawrence Stroll’s Racing Point team, before it became Aston Martin. However Stroll dropped Perez at the end of the following season and replaced him with Sebastian Vettel.

During his fourth year at Red Bull the team extended his contract by two years, then dropped him at the end of the season. He sat out the 2025 campaign before returning to F1 with Cadillac.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Gets Showcase Treatment Against Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia against Nikita Zon looks thin for a pay-per-view co-feature. Munguia supplies the name recognition, but Thursday’s press conference offered little proof that his challenger can keep the second biggest bout on Saturday’s Riyadh card competitive.

Richard Schaefer confirmed Munguia against Zon will take place immediately before Canelo Alvarez faces Christian Mbilli. That gives the WBA super middleweight title bout a prime broadcast position, yet the promotional pitch leaned on Zon entering with twelve victories and ten knockouts.

“I watched some of his fights. He’s strong, incredible power, as obviously 10 knockouts show,” Schaefer said during the media session. “I call him actually the new Siberian Rocky.”

Schaefer praised Zon’s power and stoppage record without naming a single credible opponent who proves he belongs in the ring with Munguia. Buyers heard he possesses danger, yet received zero evidence to evaluate that claim.

From a competitive standpoint, it is a gross mismatch. Munguia has logged 48 professional bouts, headlined major cards, and shared the ring with elite competition. Zon has exactly 13 fights, spent his entire career on regional Russian cards, and has never faced anyone remotely close to world class.

Slapping the moniker “the Siberian Rocky” on a completely untested fighter does not make him a threat. It is a fabricated sales gimmick designed to distract from the reality that Zon has done nothing to earn a shot at a belt on a massive international stage. Munguia should blow right through him inside five rounds, and anything less would actually look bad for Munguia.

“I came here to win and I’m leaving with nothing less than a victory. I will become the new world champion,” Zon said through a translator.

That served as his loudest quote, delivering standard bravado expected during fight week. He provided zero tactical detail on what vulnerabilities he intends to target against Munguia.

Munguia kept his comments just as brief. Asked if taking on a challenger with twelve bouts invites complacency, he pointed to his work with trainer Eddy Reynoso.

“I can just say that I’m ready. I had a great camp along Eddie. We prepared strongly,” Munguia stated through a translator. “It will be a great fight. You will see the best version of Jaime Munguia.”

The fighters offered little interest for the event. Schaefer tried filling that void by selling Zon as a raw puncher receiving a life-changing shot against an established Mexican name.

For viewers spending money on the broadcast, that pitch sounds empty. Munguia scoring a routine knockout over an untested opponent helps his record, but a premium slot requires legitimate drama. Watching an established contender cruise through a soft assignment leaves little intrigue.

As for why this fight is happening, it comes down to this. It is about keeping Munguia winning while minimizing any real risk. After picking up the WBA title against Armando Resendiz in May, his team wants him active and collecting paydays without putting him anywhere near dangerous 168-pound contenders like Osleys Iglesias, Diego Pacheco, or Hamzah Sheeraz.

Zon represents the path of least resistance for Munguia: an opponent with zero profile who will stand in front of him and provide highlight-reel footage. Boxing fans are completely exhausted by this specific brand of cynical matchmaking, which is exactly why the fight has generated virtually zero pulse online or in ticket sales.

Promoters seem to operate under the delusion that casual fans will see a gaudy knockout record, hear a goofy nickname like the “Siberian Rocky,” and instantly buy in. Today’s boxing public is far too savvy for that trick. Everyone recognizes an artificially manufactured record compiled in remote regional shows when they see one.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Gives Shakur Stevenson A Muratalla Escape Route
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley just offered Shakur Stevenson a convenient exit, one that spares him from a dangerous matchup with minimal reward. Raymond Muratalla brings serious heat without anywhere near the $15 million purse Bradley claims Stevenson wants. Stevenson could get caught, maybe even stopped, or grind out a safety-first decision that leaves fans booing anyway.

Heading back down to lightweight might not double his money, but it gives him cover. It lets him chase a different target under the banner of championship glory. Bradley basically handed him the script: drop back to 135 pounds, then unify the division.

“Now if he says, ‘I’m not going to fight him, and I’m going to go down, and I’m going to fight Zepeda for a belt,’ I’m cool with that. I’m cool with that. Stay at 135 and clean up the division. That’s what you should do,” Bradley said on his channel.

That backing carries weight while critics blast Stevenson over whether he will actually take the WBO mandate against Muratalla. Bradley opened by claiming there is “no hiding,” only to lay out the exact road map for Stevenson to walk away with his blessing.

Muratalla creates a tactical nightmare where even a victory might fail to win over frustrated fans. If Stevenson chooses to stand his ground, he gives a heavy hitter chances to connect. If he gets on his bicycle to protect the zero on his record, he only fuels the talk about being boring.

A knockout loss is a real danger here. Bradley insists he expects Stevenson to win, but picking him to prevail does not remove the physical threat, nor does it guarantee the performance builds any future buzz.

The money also looks shaky according to Bradley.

“He’s going to have to take a little bit less. It ain’t going to be $15 million. It’s going to be a lot less,” Bradley said.

From a business standpoint, retreating to lightweight makes plenty of sense. Stevenson does not even need a massive raise to justify the switch. Taking similar cash against someone his camp feels better about beats stepping into Muratalla’s crosshairs.

Dropping to 135 guarantees nothing simple, of course. Bradley’s plan means hunting down titleholders, specifically giving the green light to a tilt with William Zepeda. The real value comes down to the matchup details rather than just stepping on the scale at a lighter weight.

When a fan noted that Bradley pushed for a 135-pound return before the sanctioning body stepped in, the analyst stood firm. Stevenson can leave junior welterweight behind, but he has to plant his feet at lightweight instead of bouncing right back up after ducking Muratalla.

That bargain works for Bradley, but skeptical fight fans who want to see Muratalla get his shot will be a much tougher crowd.

Bradley supplied the public excuse by urging a chase for undisputed glory at lightweight. The real payoff is ducking a punishing clash for a paycheck that falls flat. Both realities can coexist, yet picking up another strap somewhere else will not silence the whispers about Muratalla.

Shakur’s silence is deafening, especially coming from someone who usually treats social media like a live microphone. When a fighter makes noise 24/7 about nobody wanting to get in the ring with them, going completely dark the second an actual mandatory gets called creates an awful look. It looks like battlefield freeze.

Usually, the moment a sanctioning body steps in, guys start chest-thumping about easy work, post-training clips, or talk about who is getting exposed. Instead, crickets. In combat sports, sudden radio silence often signals hesitation rather than quiet confidence. Stevenson knows Muratalla is not an aging name brought in to pad a highlight reel or a blown-up featherweight looking for a payday.

Muratalla is big, physically imposing, applies relentless forward pressure, and throws with spite. He does not care about fancy footwork or playing a game of tag to lose a decision.

Taking on a heavy-handed, high-volume puncher with everything to gain and nothing to lose requires digging into the trenches. When the reality sets in that there is no massive eight-figure check waiting on the other side to justify that kind of physical punishment, battle nerves kick in fast.

Right now, his camp is likely running the numbers and looking for every possible exit route. Dropping back down to 135 to claim an undisputed crown sounds a lot more heroic in a press release than admitting you want no part of an absolute buzzsaw at 140.

Sports.title: Richard Schaefer Oversells Canelo Alvarez’s Christian Mbilli Choice
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez looks to have picked the softer option in Christian Mbilli, though nobody expects an easy night at the office. Mbilli gives Canelo clear lanes to time counters, letting him steal rounds on the scorecards even if he gets outworked. Osleys Iglesias, on the other hand, represents a far more unforgiving matchup.

Promoter Richard Schaefer repeatedly praised Canelo at Thursday’s final press conference for picking Mbilli to give fans the best fight possible. That narrative ignored how slim the pool really was. With WBA titlist Jaime Munguia practically off the table due to gym loyalty, plus a vacant WBO belt, Canelo really only had Mbilli or IBF champion Iglesias to consider.

“Because I do not believe in shortcuts. I have been a champion for many years. I just want to fight the best,” Canelo said when asked about the decision.

Even if Mbilli throws a hundred punches a round, Canelo knows how judges score fights. A crisp, explosive counter shot that snaps an opponent’s head back often wins rounds over flurry work that lands to the body, head, or gloves. Against Mbilli, Canelo has a clear path to win rounds on the cards.

Iglesias is an entirely different problem, and arguably a far more punishing one. The Cuban is a rangy, hard-hitting southpaw who controls real estate with a stiff jab and detonates with a lead right hook. Canelo struggling against disciplined boxers with length and movement is well established.

Following Iglesias around the ring while absorbing straight lefts, right hooks, and jabs would be grueling, with very few clean openings to fire back. Iglesias brings real knockout danger without needing to smother himself on the inside to get it. Iglesias brings the bigger punch, but he also possesses the technical skill to dominate without hunting for a knockout.

Canelo risks trailing, missing, and soaking up damage without landing enough in return to keep pace. Reaching the final bell would still leave him battered. That is a projection, yet the Cuban’s length, precision, and power make it a very real danger.

Mbilli brings heat of his own. His swarm could pin Canelo against the ropes for long stretches. The difference is that Mbilli’s relentless forward motion keeps him squarely in range for Canelo’s signature counter rights and body hooks.

That gives Canelo a realistic path to victory. Mbilli can throw and land three as many punches, but judges often reward Canelo’s cleaner, harder single shots. Activity does not guarantee points, and Mbilli will offer plenty of targets for flashier work.

Canelo would get far fewer looks against Iglesias. He would need to evade the jab, close the gap, and connect before Iglesias moves away or fires back with something harder.

“I just need to be myself, and that is how I am going to win this fight,” Mbilli stated.

He could be right. Mbilli’s furious engine could easily overwhelm the veteran if Canelo cannot punch with enough authority to slow him down. Calling him the better option is far from guaranteeing a Canelo win.

Canelo never admitted to dodging Iglesias over stylistic concerns, and this remains a personal breakdown of the matchup. Still, Schaefer’s spin invites a reality check. Between the two champions on the table, Canelo selected the opponent who gives him room to land and a much clearer route to a victory on the cards.

It still could be controversial if Canelo wins a decision against Mbilli, but at least he would see the final bell, and his face wouldn’t be as beat up as it would be against Iglesias.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley’s Canelo Massacre Pick Ignores Reality
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley expects Canelo Alvarez to completely destroy Christian Mbilli, but that forecast fits the fighter Canelo used to be, not the one we see in the ring today. While his counterpunching remains lethal, blowing out an energetic pressure fighter requires relentless, high-gear output that recent outings just do not support.

Bradley argues that veteran savvy and sharp timing will punish Mbilli’s defensive flaws. That prediction hinges on Canelo avoiding the ropes and dictating action in the center of the ring.

“Canelo by massacre. Canelo by massacre. That’s what I got. He might even stop him,” Bradley said on Into the Storm. “Canelo is not gonna throw more punches than Mbilli, but his punches gonna be way more accurate, way more sound, way more placed than Mbilli.”

Bradley points to a glaring habit in Mbilli’s approach. When Mbilli bites on feints, he tends to dip his head and stare at the canvas, opening himself up to clean hooks and uppercuts. The expectation is that Canelo will time those flaws, threading counters through the incoming storm to force a late stoppage.

Still, even peak Canelo rarely battered elite competition into submission the way Bradley imagines. Older versions of Shane Mosley and Miguel Cotto went the full twelve. Gennadiy Golovkin lasted thirty-six rounds with him across three meetings, including the trilogy finale when Golovkin was forty. Different styles produce different results, but boxing history shows that defensive openings do not immediately guarantee a blowout.

Bradley fought in that very same era, so his viewpoint might lean on respect for his peer group. That does not discount his technical breakdown, but it does raise questions about whether his prediction relies on an outdated version of the Mexican star.

Seeing an opening is completely different from exploiting it through twelve fast-paced rounds. Canelo might spot the exact counter he wants, yet lack the stamina to deliver it over and over. A single crisp shot might turn heads, but it will not magically halt the next wave of pressure if Canelo cannot command real estate.

“As long as Canelo keep his back up off the ropes and keep the fight in the center of the ring,” Bradley added, suggesting Canelo should handle the assignment smoothly.

The eye test over the past few years undercuts any idea that Canelo is going to command the center of the ring against a relentless motor like Mbilli. Ever since the Jermell Charlo fight, Canelo’s legs have steadily abandoned him. What used to be deliberate ring generalship has turned into an older fighter looking for a place to lean.

Once the clock hits round six, his default setting is backing straight into the ropes, shelling up behind the high guard, and letting the ropes do the work of keeping him upright.

Against Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga, William Scull, and Terence Crawford, that exact pattern played out. Canelo cannot sustain footwork to dictate geography anymore, and he certainly lacks the conditioning to maintain the work rate required to keep an aggressive dog off his chest. His stamina dictates that he fights in brief, explosive bursts, spending the remaining two minutes of every round resting and waiting to time a single big counter.

That strategy works when hand-picking opponents who either freeze under the lights or lack the punch volume and inside craft to make him pay for taking rounds off. Munguia had the volume but zero defensive awareness or punching power; Berlanga was hesitant and limited; Scull had nowhere near the offensive pop or pedigree to capitalize. They were tailor-made style matchups designed to let Canelo coast on reputation and single heavy shots.

Mbilli is the complete opposite of a hand-picked rest stop. He does not care about getting countered; he never stops throwing, and he thrives precisely where Canelo now camps out: on the inside, chest-to-chest, hammering away at the ribs and arms.

If Canelo’s only plan is to retreat to the ropes and look for single uppercuts while Mbilli fires non-stop for twelve rounds, relying on the judges to favor low-volume potshots is going to be a very dangerous game.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Reveals Shakur Stevenson Vanished After Ring Stunt
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson gathered all the buzz for a potential O’Shaquie Foster bout without stepping into the ring. By stepping through the ropes following Foster’s win over Raymond Ford in May, Stevenson ignited major public anticipation. Yet Foster reveals his team pushed for the bout, waited, and met total silence.

That recent past demands a sharper look at Stevenson’s latest words. Foster just took down Emanuel Navarrete, and Stevenson quickly voiced fresh interest. Boxing enthusiasts ought to pause before celebrating, keeping Foster’s prior experience in mind.

“We kept asking. We didn’t hear nothing. We didn’t hear nothing,” Foster said on the Ariel Helwani show. “We held out for a little bit. We didn’t hear nothing. Tyrone didn’t hear nothing.”

Foster explained that talks never progressed to discussing weight classes. He expressed total readiness to step up to lightweight or junior welterweight, clearing away a major hurdle for a 130-pound titleholder looking upward.

“We didn’t even get that far, but I didn’t care,” Foster noted. “Like, I honestly didn’t care whether it was 135, 140. Either one. It didn’t matter to me.”

It looked like pure clout chasing from Shakur, plain and simple. Walking into another man’s spotlight right after a hard-earned victory creates the illusion that you want the fight next. Fans get excited, the broadcast cameras lock onto you, and you get all the free publicity without taking an ounce of risk. Then, the second Foster’s camp actually reached out to make the fight happen, Shakur vanished into thin air. Total silence.

Once Foster beat Navarrete, Stevenson offered public compliments along with a fresh challenge.

“Hell of a fighter. He will never give me my credit, but I’ll be real tonight. He showed his level,” Stevenson stated in a social post read on air. “That’s a challenge that would get me out of bed. Let’s do it whenever he’s ready. I’ll be here after his undisputed run.”

That is what makes Stevenson’s latest comment after Foster beat Navarrete look so empty. Saying he will fight Foster “whenever he’s ready” completely flips the reality of what happened. Foster was ready months ago, even offering to jump up in weight to make it effortless for Stevenson. Shakur was the one who went missing.

For now, Foster’s sights remain locked on unifying all four belts at 130 pounds. Chasing undisputed status puts Foster in control rather than hanging on Shakur’s schedule. Foster can hunt the remaining belt while Stevenson figures out whether his online comments translate into real business.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Gives PBC More Years Without Becoming A Star
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is locking in more of his prime with PBC, even though his run with the outfit has not turned him into a household name. He has collected belts in three divisions. Casual fans still have little reason to tune in, and facing Michal Cieslak on December 5 will not change that.

Benavidez turns thirty next year. He burned through his twenties chasing Canelo Alvarez. Then he cleared out of light heavyweight without ever facing Dmitry Bivol or Artur Beterbiev. Now he sits at cruiserweight, stacking belts while marquee opponents remain out of reach.

“I’ve always wanted to stay with PBC. I feel like what we’ve built, obviously PBC is PBC before I got there, but the work I’ve put in for this promotional company, I’m not going to get that anywhere else,” Benavidez told FightHubTV. “I feel comfortable with Luis De Cubas. I feel comfortable with Al Haymon. This is my family. I’m one of the pillars that helps PBC stand.”

He sounds like someone trapped by sunk costs. Pouring years into a promotional stable is no reason to surrender the rest of his career. If mainstream fame is the actual target, he needs to look honestly at what loyalty has given him.

He has put on solid bouts. Caleb Plant provided genuine heat. Demetrius Andrade came undefeated. David Morrell was a dangerous test. Gilberto Ramirez offered the chance to pick up cruiserweight hardware. The resume is legitimate.

The box office numbers tell a different story. Reports put the Morrell clash at 150,000 to 160,000 pay-per-view buys. The Andrade fight reportedly landed around 60,000 buys. Those figures are not official numbers, but they prove he has not developed into an elite pay-per-view draw.

Canelo was the matchup that could have launched him into superstardom. It never happened, even with both fighters under the PBC umbrella. Canelo walked his own road, while Benavidez paid the bill in wasted time. Sharing a promotional banner provided zero leverage to force the biggest draw into the ring.

Bivol chose his own path too, giving up the WBC belt rather than facing Benavidez in 2025. Promoters cannot force anyone to sign. Yet Benavidez is the one creeping toward thirty without those career-defining names on his record.

Cieslak brings another strap to the table, but offers zero buzz for American fans. Winning might give Benavidez three cruiserweight titles, yet leave him completely invisible to general sports culture. That is the exact loop he must break.

Launching DB Promotions once his deal with Sampson Lewkowicz wraps up gives him real leverage. Sticking with PBC feels familiar, but familiarity seems to be his main motivation for staying put.

Benavidez has shown he can win titles with this team. He has not shown he can become a crossover sensation with them. Betting the remainder of his peak on this same routine is risky. He needs Jai Opetaia or another opponent people will actually pay to watch. Cieslak is just another belt while the real clock keeps ticking.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Documentary Launches on Netflix Ahead of Joshua Fight
Sports.content:
Netflix releases TYSON FURY on November 27, tracing the heavyweight’s rise through boxing and examining his personal struggles before he faces Anthony Joshua on December 11.

Lucy Wilcox directs the feature-length documentary. Fury, his wife Paris and father John give interviews alongside previously unseen footage from his life and career.

Tyson Fury’s Career and Family Life

The film follows Fury from childhood into the heavyweight ranks, revisiting the victories and setbacks that shaped his career. His family contributes its accounts of the experiences behind those performances.

Mental health, addiction and the loss of a child are among the subjects covered. The documentary also examines Fury’s views on masculinity, his family relationships and the support he has relied on throughout his career.

Paris and John bring their perspectives to a film that explores the personal pressures accompanying Fury’s success in the ring.

Fury vs Joshua: December 11 Date and Netflix Broadcast

Fury and Joshua step into opposite corners on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales. Netflix will broadcast their first professional meeting globally to all members at no additional cost.

The remaining bouts have yet to be announced.

At their September 30 press conference, Fury spoke about the years spent waiting to get Joshua into the ring.

“I’m looking forward to the challenge. It’s been 10 years in the making,” Fury said.

“The rise has been phenomenal from both fighters. We’ve both had our ups and downs. Finally, we arrive at this moment.”

Fury also praised his British rival: “He’s been a role model and a poster boy for British boxing for years.”

Joshua welcomed the occasion and said their exchanges would drive him through extra rounds in the gym.

“I feel fresh. I feel very excited about this opportunity to work again,” Joshua said.

Ghana News.title: Stable economy, cheaper credit key to youth jobs — BoG Governor
Ghana News.content:
Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama

The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, says falling lending rates and stronger private sector credit growth are among the gains from recent macroeconomic management efforts, creating improved conditions for businesses to access financing and expand operations.

He said the average lending rate declined from 30.25 per cent in December 2024 to 15.78 per cent in September 2026, while growth in real private sector credit rose sharply from 0.20 per cent to 26.42 per cent over the same period.

Dr Asiama announced the figures at the launch of the maiden edition of Ghana in Numbers 2025, a publication by the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS), on Thursday, October 29.

He said the figures reflected improvements in credit conditions, alongside a sustained decline in inflation, relative stability in the exchange rate and greater resilience in the banking sector.

The Governor said maintaining a stable macroeconomic environment and a well-functioning financial system was important to expanding economic opportunities, particularly for young people seeking employment or looking to establish businesses.

Credit conditions improve

Dr Asiama said the gains recorded in the economy over the past couple of years were helping to create conditions for productive economic activity.

He noted that inflation had remained in single digits for 13 consecutive months, while the exchange rate had been relatively stable despite external pressures.

He also pointed to improvements in the resilience of the banking sector, which he said complemented the broader efforts to stabilise the economy.

The decline in average lending rates, from 30.25 per cent at the end of 2024 to 15.78 per cent in September 2026, represented a significant change in the cost of borrowing over the period.

At the same time, real private sector credit growth strengthened from 0.20 per cent in December 2024 to 26.42 per cent in September 2026.

The figures, he said, pointed to improved credit conditions that could support businesses and other productive activities.

Youth potential needs investment

Beyond the economic indicators, Dr Asiama said Ghana's large youth population offered considerable potential for innovation and entrepreneurship, but realising that potential would require deliberate investment in skills and enterprise development.

He said young people needed relevant training, access to opportunities and an environment that encouraged investment and business growth.

Achieving those objectives, he added, would require coordinated action informed by reliable data on the circumstances of young people, the gaps in opportunities available to them and the policies needed to address those gaps.

He said Ghana in Numbers could support that process by bringing demographic, social and economic information together to inform national debate and policy decisions.

The Governor also highlighted the importance of access to finance in helping young people turn business ideas into viable enterprises.

Expanding financial inclusion

Dr Asiama said the Bank of Ghana was pursuing complementary initiatives to improve financial inclusion and financial health while encouraging responsible innovation in the financial sector.

The initiatives are intended to make formal financial services more accessible, affordable and convenient, particularly for young people, women, micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and underserved communities.

He said a stable economy and an effective financial system were important to ensuring that more people and businesses could participate in productive economic activity.

The Governor urged stakeholders to view Ghana in Numbers 2025 as more than a statistical publication, describing it as a national resource for assessing the country's circumstances, measuring progress and making informed decisions about the future.

He congratulated the GSS, its Governing Board and Management, as well as the institutions and individuals who contributed to the publication.

Dr Asiama expressed the hope that the report would become a trusted national reference for strengthening transparency, supporting evidence-based policymaking and promoting a more productive and inclusive economy, particularly for young people.

Ghana News.title: BoG turns to AI to strengthen financial-sector oversight
Ghana News.content:
Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama

The Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has called for a dedicated digital platform to make the country’s official statistics more accessible, saying wider access to reliable data could improve economic research, policymaking and investment decisions.

He said making underlying data available in machine-readable formats would allow researchers, policymakers and businesses to deploy artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning and other analytical tools to identify economic trends and relationships that might not be apparent from published tables and charts.

Dr Asiama made the call at the launch of the maiden edition of Ghana in Numbers 2025, an initiative of the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS), on Thursday, October 29.

He commended the GSS for bringing together authoritative information on the country’s socio-economic conditions, describing the report as an important resource for understanding national progress, identifying emerging challenges and setting development priorities.

He said the publication would be particularly useful if official statistics were made easier for policymakers, businesses, researchers, development partners and the public to access and use.

Data at the heart of monetary policy

Dr Asiama said accurate and timely statistics were essential to the central bank’s work, particularly in setting monetary policy and regulating the financial sector.

As an inflation-targeting central bank, he said, the BoG relied on data to assess price movements and their relationship with exchange rates, economic activity, credit conditions and developments in the external sector.

Such assessments, he explained, required sound economic research and analytical methods supported by reliable statistics.

“Reliable statistics do more than inform policy. They strengthen transparency, enhance accountability and promote public confidence in institutions,” he said.

He added that dependable economic data also helped businesses and investors assess prevailing conditions, manage risks and make informed investment decisions.

The Governor welcomed the inclusion of a dedicated monetary and financial-sector section in Ghana in Numbers 2025, which draws substantially on official data produced by the BoG.

Information on inflation, interest rates, lending to businesses and households, foreign reserves and banking-sector conditions, he said, offered a clearer picture of the country’s economic and financial environment.

Push for AI-driven economic analysis

Dr Asiama said advances in data science, artificial intelligence and machine learning presented opportunities to improve economic forecasting, identify patterns and assess risks.

He noted that these technologies could complement conventional economic analysis and strengthen the central bank’s ability to respond to changing economic conditions.

To realise those benefits, however, he said the data underpinning publications such as Ghana in Numbers needed to be available in formats that could be readily accessed and analysed electronically.

A dedicated portal offering machine-readable datasets, he said, would allow researchers, academics and policymakers to examine information in greater depth and investigate relationships across different economic indicators.

The proposed platform could extend the usefulness of the report beyond its published tables and charts by allowing users to conduct their own analysis using advanced digital tools.

BoG builds capacity, prepares AI rules

Dr Asiama said the central bank was strengthening its own capacity to use data analytics and emerging technologies in policy development and institutional decision-making.

As part of that effort, the BoG has established a Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Department to improve data governance, expand analytical capabilities and support the responsible use of new technologies.

He also disclosed that the bank was developing a directive to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the financial sector.

The proposed directive, he said, formed part of the central bank’s approach to encouraging innovation while addressing risks associated with the growing use of AI.

His remarks highlighted the importance of combining reliable official statistics with modern analytical tools to strengthen economic decision-making, while ensuring that the use of emerging technologies in the financial system is appropriately governed.

Ghana News.title: The Breast that feeds the future: Nurture it, Protect it, Check it
Ghana News.content:
By Dorcas Zenabu Seidu

Why breastfeeding and breast cancer are one story, and why women and men must both read it

In the first hour of life, a mother’s breast delivers colostrum, the baby’s first vaccine. Over the next six months it can supply everything a child needs. It is one of the most powerful public health tools we have. It is also the site of the cancer most often diagnosed in Ghanaian women, and, surprisingly, one that men can get too. This is one organ and one story: how we nurture it, how we protect it, and why we must keep checking it.

Nurture it: the first hour and the first six months

WHO and UNICEF recommend starting breastfeeding within one hour of birth, the Golden Hour. Skin-to-skin contact steadies the newborn’s temperature and breathing and helps the mother’s womb contract, lowering the risk of postpartum bleeding. Colostrum coats the baby’s gut with antibodies, so delaying it is a missed dose of the strongest immune protection the child will ever get from this source. WHO estimates that close to 400,000 deaths in children under five could be prevented each year if infants were exclusively breastfed for six months and breastfed on to two years. Mothers gain too: every 12 months of breastfeeding lowers breast cancer risk by about 4.3%, and breastfeeding is linked to lower cardiovascular risk. For families, it removes the cost of formula, which in many homes rivals the rent. Formula remains a vital option when breastfeeding is truly not possible, but routine use without clean water and sterilisation raises the risk of infection.

Make it possible: families, workplaces and policy

Support has not kept pace with the science. The extended-family help that once carried new mothers has thinned, and many return to work long before six months. The ILO sets a floor of just 14 weeks of maternity leave and the global average is about 17–18 weeks, which ends well short of the six months WHO recommends. That standard is a labour compromise, not a clinical target. We need at least six months of paid leave, lactation rooms and paid express breaks, crèches near the workplace, and supportive managers. Employers who do this report lower turnover and absenteeism. We must also say plainly that the breast’s first purpose is to feed a child, not to belong to a husband or to modesty. And when a mother does not survive childbirth, a prepared system matters: pasteurised donor milk first, a screened wet nurse next, safe formula with real support last, with skin-to-skin care from a caregiver throughout.

The same organ, a different battle

Everything above assumes the breast is healthy. In 2022, Ghana recorded 5,026 new cases of breast cancer and 2,369 deaths, nearly one death for every two diagnoses. Breast cancer makes up about three in every ten cancers in Ghanaian women, and the average age at diagnosis is 49, some thirteen years younger than in Caucasian populations. Reports differ, from about 70% to over 80%, but most women arrive with advanced disease. These are mothers in the middle of raising children and holding households together. A country cannot claim to invest in the next generation while neglecting the organ that feeds it. When a mother is lost to late diagnosis, a baby may lose milk, closeness, and protection. The link runs both ways: breastfeeding lowers risk, but it is protection, not immunity, and a lump that persists in a lactating breast must never be dismissed as “too much milk.”

The plot twist: men have breasts too

Breast cancer is not only a women’s disease. About 0.5–1% of breast cancers occur in men, and a leading Ghanaian specialist puts the local figure at 1–3%. Few men know this, so a small lump behind the nipple may be ignored for months. With so little breast tissue, the cancer reaches the chest wall sooner, and men are often diagnosed later. Risk factors include age, family history, BRCA2 and BRCA1 gene changes, Klinefelter syndrome, obesity, liver disease, and heavy alcohol use. Men are also partners: a man who knows the signs can notice a change in his wife, urge her to be checked, and stand by her through treatment.

Know the signs, the risks, and the myths

Early breast cancer often has no symptoms, which is why checking matters. When there are signs, they include:

A new lump or thickening in the breast or armpit, usually painless

A change in the size or shape of the breast

Dimpling, puckering, or thickened “orange-peel” skin; redness or scaling

A nipple turning inward, or bloodstained nipple discharge

Pain is not the test. About half of breast cancers occur in women with no risk factor beyond being female and growing older, so having no family history is no reassurance. Risk rises with age, family history, inherited gene changes, obesity, alcohol, tobacco, inactivity, and long-term postmenopausal hormones. Nothing guarantees prevention, but a healthy weight, regular activity, less alcohol, no smoking, and breastfeeding all help. Screening does not stop cancer from forming; it stops it being found late. Four myths to retire:

Myth: “It is witchcraft or a curse.” Fact: It is a disease of abnormal cells. Faith can walk beside treatment, never replace it.

“It is witchcraft or a curse.” It is a disease of abnormal cells. Faith can walk beside treatment, never replace it. Myth: “It is a death sentence.” Fact: It is treatable, and most effectively when found early.

“It is a death sentence.” It is treatable, and most effectively when found early. Myth: “No pain, no problem,” or “No family history, no risk.” Fact: Lumps are often painless, and most women diagnosed have no known family history.

“No pain, no problem,” or “No family history, no risk.” Lumps are often painless, and most women diagnosed have no known family history. Myth: “Only women get it.” Fact: Men do too, and any male breast lump needs examination.

Check yourself, then keep checking

Self-examination is about breast awareness: knowing your normal so you notice change early. Do it once a month, about a week after your period, or on a fixed date if you no longer have periods, or are pregnant or breastfeeding.

Look in a mirror with your arms down, raised, and hands on your hips, for changes in size, shape, skin, or nipple. Feel, standing or lying down, pressing the pads of three fingers in small circles over the whole breast, from collarbone to bra line and armpit to breastbone. Check the nipple by gently squeezing it for discharge. Men use the same method around the nipple.

Self-examination builds awareness; it does not replace professional checks. Guidance shared in Ghana’s awareness campaigns advises a clinical breast examination every three years under 35 and every year from 35, and a baseline mammogram from 40, earlier with a strong family history. A clear result today says nothing about next year, so keep checking. Most lumps turn out not to be cancer, but only a trained health worker can tell. Go early, and not to a prayer camp or herbalist first.

A shared commitment

Protecting the breast, as a source of life and as a part of the body that can fall ill, take action at every level:

Families: share the load so mothers can nurse, drop the myths about breast “ownership,” encourage every woman and man to be checked, and stand beside anyone who is diagnosed.

share the load so mothers can nurse, drop the myths about breast “ownership,” encourage every woman and man to be checked, and stand beside anyone who is diagnosed. Communities: normalise public nursing, support human milk banking, and end the stigma and the witchcraft narrative surrounding breast cancer that keep people from seeking care.

normalise public nursing, support human milk banking, and end the stigma and the witchcraft narrative surrounding breast cancer that keep people from seeking care. Employers: provide lactation rooms, paid breaks, and nearby crèches, and add breast screening to staff wellness programmes.

provide lactation rooms, paid breaks, and nearby crèches, and add breast screening to staff wellness programmes. Health Facilities: Inculcate breast cancer awareness and examination into routine service delivery. Make this critical service accessible all year-round and not just a one-month celebration

Inculcate breast cancer awareness and examination into routine service delivery. Make this critical service accessible all year-round and not just a one-month celebration Health Authorities: Set up a national cancer data repository to make information readily available and show a clear picture of our cancer situation.

Set up a national cancer data repository to make information readily available and show a clear picture of our cancer situation. Governments: legislate at least six months of paid maternity leave, with meaningful paternity leave, and make breast screening, diagnosis, and treatment accessible and affordable.

Three things to do this week as we wrap up the Pick October:

(1) examine yourself;

(2) book your clinical breast examination if one is due;

(3) tell one person, man or woman, what you have read.

The breast nurtures the future. Let us make sure it lives to see that future.

Sources: WHO (Breast cancer; Infant and young child feeding); GLOBOCAN 2022, IARC (Ghana); Victora et al., The Lancet, 2016; Collaborative Group on Hormonal Factors in Breast Cancer, The Lancet, 2002; ILO Maternity Protection Convention No. 183; Ghanaian Times, Graphic Online, and Citi Newsroom reports on breast cancer in Ghana (2025); Breast Care International.

Dorcas Zenabu Seidu, Program Manager, Public Health Nursing – ODNMS, GHS #asisterthinkingoutloud

Ghana News.title: Anas announces exposé on Angela List’s Nguvu/Konongo Mines
Ghana News.content:
Investigative journalist Anas Aremeyaw Anas is preparing to publish an investigation into the operations of Nguvu/Konongo Mines, owned by Angela List, with a focus on the dispute surrounding the mining interests and its possible implications for Ghana’s gold sector.

The investigation, titled The Stakes and Mystery of Angela List’s Nguvu/Konongo Mines, is being undertaken by The New Crusading Guide in collaboration with Tiger Eye.

In a Facebook post on Thursday, October 29, 2026, Anas said the investigation was based on documents, court records and other material gathered by the investigative teams.

He suggested that the findings would examine issues surrounding the mining operations, including the relationships behind them and the potential consequences for the state.

“The New Crusading Guide and Tiger Eye peered behind the gold veil. What we found sits in documents, in court records, and in places no one wanted us to look,” he wrote.

Questions over Ghana’s gold sector

Anas said the investigation would explore how the dispute was affecting the country's gold industry and what financial implications it might have for the state.

He also indicated that the report would examine the networks and relationships associated with the mining operations.

“How is the fight reshaping Ghana’s gold sector and what is the state losing while it rages on? What networks and relationships underpin List’s operations? Who and who are behind. We unmask and break it down,” he stated.

The journalist did not provide details of the specific findings or identify the individuals who might feature in the investigation.

He said further information, including names and figures, would be made available when the full report was released.

“Some stories are reported. This one had to be dug out. No names yet. No numbers yet. Just this: when the full file opens, a lot of people will be reading it twice and some will wish it had never been written,” he added.

Ghana News.title: Leonant Yert retains position as Most Outstanding PR Agency
Ghana News.content:
Leonant Yert Ltd has been named the “Most Outstanding Public Relations Agency (PR Consultancy of the Year)” for the 2025 review period at the 2026 Institute of Public Relations (IPR), PR Ghana Excellence Awards.

This latest recognition strengthens Leonant Yert’s position as the leading Public Relations consultancy in Ghana and validates the Firm’s previous winning of the same award for the 2023-2024 review period. The back-to-back recognition also underscores the Consultancy’s commitment to delivering strategic communication, reputation management, issues and crisis management and stakeholder engagement solutions that create measurable value for its clients.

According to the IPR’s Professional Awards Committee, Leonant Yert’s selection as the best was based on its exceptional work, demonstrated through strategic leadership and measurable results delivered during the review period.

The award was received by Isaac Kusi and Alberta James, both Account Managers of the Firm at the recently concluded 2026 National Public Relations Summit and Awards in Koforidua. The event which was held under the theme, “Public Relations and Leadership Readiness” brought together public relations practitioners, corporate leaders and other stakeholders to examine the evolving role of the profession and recognise excellence in communication practice.

The annual PR Excellence Awards is IPR Ghana’s platform for recognising exceptional work, encouraging continuous improvement and strengthening the public relations profession in Ghana. The Awards highlight achievements across PR consultancies, independent practitioners, corporate communications teams, government agencies, NGOs and other organisations.

Speaking on this achievement, Chief Executive Officer and Account Team Lead at Leonant Yert, Nii Okai Nunoo said, “retaining the Most Outstanding Public Relations Agency award, is testimony to the great collaboration that exists between our clients and us and also within our team. It also shows the commitment and diligence that we at Leonant Yert and our clients have invested in developing and executing solutions which improve our clients’ performance and reputation and ultimately give the stakeholders of our various clients the assurance they need.”

“At Leonant Yert, we believe that true value is built when organisations demonstrate reliability through their actions. Our role is to help bridge the gap between what organisations say and do and what their stakeholders experience; giving stakeholders tangible reasons to be confident and assured of our clients’ reliability and guaranteeing the expected outcomes”, he added.

Mr Nunoo expressed gratitude to Leonant Yert’s clients and partners for their continued confidence and support, describing their trust as an important part of the Firm’s success.

Established in 2016, Leonant Yert is a multiple award winning public relations and communications firm providing a full-suite service within Ghana and with the capability to undertake projects across the rest of Africa.

Leonant Yert operates under the brand promise “building true value”, with an emphasis on improving assurance for its clients, through trust, collaboration, creativity, and professional service. The Firm’s signature offering focuses on protecting, building, and projecting the business and reputation of its clients. This covers the key service areas of business support, public policy, and organisational effectiveness.

Through its work, Leonant Yert supports corporate entities, individuals and organisations to navigate communication challenges, strengthen stakeholder relationships, build credible, trusted reputations and ultimately improve corporate performance. Its approach focuses on ensuring that communication and engagement deliver more than visibility by helping clients demonstrate value, manage risks, maintain stakeholder confidence and remain prepared when outcomes matter.

Ghana News.title: Communications Minister Sam George confirmed as chair of AU STC on Communication and ICT
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George (MP), has been confirmed as Chair of the African Union Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT (AU STC-ICT) at its 6th Ordinary Session in Libreville, Gabon.

In his opening address to the ministerial session, the Minister described the chairmanship as a responsibility to the entire African Union, emphasising the need for stronger continental cooperation to accelerate Africa’s digital transformation.

“I accept such responsibility not as a privilege for one country, but as a duty to our entire union,” he said.

Addressing Africa’s digital priorities, Hon. George called for a decisive shift from policy development to implementation, noting that the continent already has key frameworks on digital transformation, artificial intelligence and data governance.

“What we have too often lacked is the collective will to implement them at the pace that our people demand,” he stated.

He highlighted connectivity, data governance, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence as critical areas requiring coordinated action, stressing that Africa must take a more active role in shaping the global digital economy.

“When we negotiate alone, we are 55 separate markets, but when we negotiate together, we are a market of nearly 1.5 billion people,” he said, adding that Africa must be “at the table, not on the menu” in global conversations on artificial intelligence, data and digital trade.

The Minister also underscored the importance of equipping Africa’s young population with the skills and opportunities to innovate, drawing attention to Ghana’s One Million Coders Programme as an example of what young people can achieve when given the right tools.

Setting out his priorities for the chairmanship, Hon. George pledged to build consensus, strengthen cooperation and drive implementation across the continent.

“Over the next two years, this committee must be measured not by the declarations that we adopt, but by the results that we deliver,” he said.

He called on member states to take bold decisions towards a shared digital future in which Africa can operate as one digital market and speak with one digital voice.

Ghana’s chairmanship comes at a critical time as African countries work to expand digital access, strengthen cybersecurity, advance responsible AI development and ensure that the continent’s digital resources and opportunities serve its people.

Ghana News.title: Patrick Stewart, best known for “Star Trek” and “X-Men,” dies at 86
Ghana News.content:
Legendary actor Sir Patrick Stewart, best known for his work in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises and his prolific award-winning stage career, has died at 86 years old, his spokesperson confirmed.

Stewart died at home on Wednesday, spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak said in a statement. His death followed "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia," Novak said.

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Novak said.

Stewart began his acting career doing stage plays in the United Kingdom, joining the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s.

Stewart's most recognizable role began in 1987, when he started playing Enterprise Captain Jean-Luc Picard on "Star Trek: The Next Generation." The show ran for seven seasons and also spawned four "Star Trek" films featuring Stewart as Picard and the rest of the "Next Generation" cast. Stewart later reprised the role for Paramount+ series "Star Trek: Picard," which ran for three seasons.

Fellow "Star Trek" legend William Shatner posted: "Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor. From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work."

George Takei, who played Hikaru Sulu in the original "Star Trek" series, said on Threads that "Stewart took the starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before, and he inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity. Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain."

Stewart also played "X-Men" leader Charles Xavier in over half a dozen films in the "X-Men" franchise. He reprised the role for the upcoming "Avengers: Doomsday," which will be released in December 2026. Marvel Studios said on social media that it was "deeply saddened" by Stewart's passing, calling him a "singular talent" who defined the character "for generations of fans."

"X-Men" co-star Hugh Jackman said in a social media post "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today. And, in my book, a tremendous friend and man. I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."

Stewart appeared in dozens of other film and television roles, including voice work on Seth MacFarlane's animated shows "Family Guy" and "American Dad."

"Patrick was one of those icons who we somehow all took for granted would always be with us," MacFarlane wrote on social media Thursday. "... He was that rare actor who could take any bit of dialogue and elevate it, making a good writer sound great, and a great writer sound masterful. He was also as humble as they come ... We have lost a legendary actor today, and for many of us, a good friend. He will be deeply missed by the entire planet."

The bulk of Stewart's work was on the stage: He was a frequent presence on Broadway and in London's West End, where he played characters from Shakespearean villains to Charles Dickens' Ebenezer Scrooge. He appeared with "X-Men" co-star Ian McKellen in "Waiting for Godot" in London in 2010, then again in New York City in 2013. He also performed his one-man version of "A Christmas Carol" frequently over the decades.

Stewart appeared in over 60 Royal Shakespeare Company productions. The company named him an "Honorary Associate Artist" to celebrate his contributions to their work. He has also been awarded three Olivier Awards for his London stage performances and received one Tony nomination for his work on Broadway.

Stewart was nominated for multiple Emmy, Golden Globe and SAG awards for his on-screen roles. He won a Grammy Award in 1995 for "Best Spoken Word Album for Children."

In 2001, Queen Elizabeth II appointed Stewart an Officer of the Order of the British Empire. In 2010, Stewart received a knighthood, again from Elizabeth II, for his services to drama.

In 2023, Stewart published the memoir "Making It So." The book landed him on the New York Times' best-sellers list. He also recorded a companion audiobook.

Stewart was actively working until 2026. In addition to his role in "Avengers: Doomsday," he recorded an audiobook where he narrated and commented on all 154 of William Shakespeare's sonnets. He also had a voice role in the animated comedy "The Sheep Detectives."

Stewart was married three times. He wed Sheila Falconer in 1966. The pair had two children — Daniel and Sophia — before divorcing in 1990. From 2000 to 2003, he was married to producer Wendy Neuss. In 2008, he began dating singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell. The two married in 2013 and were wed until his death. Novak said Ozell was at Stewart's side when he died.

Stewart was also "a fierce advocate for causes he strongly believed in," his spokesperson said. Those causes included social justice, women's rights, domestic abuse advocacy, veterans' rights, the refugee crisis, animal rights and political reform.

"We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace," Novak said. "His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre. … He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life."

Ghana News.title: Court remands four over Worawora disturbances
Ghana News.content:
The Dambai Circuit Court has remanded four people to police custody over their alleged involvement in disturbances at Dwabrem-Worawora in the Oti Region.

The accused are Kwame Aboagye Ahenkora, 55, Prince Asante, 27, Daniel Wiafe, 20, and Kwabena Nsimbo, 22.

Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) John Nchor, Public Affairs Officer of the Oti Regional Police Command, said the accused persons would reappear before the Court on November 17, 2026.

He said the alleged disturbances occurred at Dwabrem on October 24, 2026, amid tensions over the commencement of rites for the Akwantutenten Festival.

DSP Nchor said the incident allegedly involved the burning of vehicle tyres and other acts of violence following claims that a High Court injunction had been secured to restrain the celebration.

He said Police personnel deployed to the area extinguished the fire and restored order.

DSP Nchor said the Oti Regional Security Council (REGSEC), at a meeting with representatives of the disputing families on October 26, directed the parties to seek redress through the courts and the Houses of Chiefs.

He said the Council stressed that the chieftaincy dispute must be resolved through lawful means and directed that all persons arrested in connection with the disturbances be dealt with in accordance with the law.

DSP Nchor said the Oti Regional Police Command had appealed to all parties to remain calm, exercise restraint and respect lawful processes to help maintain peace and security in Worawora.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
