The commission’s Executive Secretary, Oluwabukola Adeyemo, said anyone intending to drill a borehole or extract groundwater must first obtain the required permits.

“Drilling or abstracting groundwater without LASWARCO authorisation is illegal and punishable under the Law,” Ms Adeyemo said.

She stated that the commission would seal facilities operating without the required authorisation and prosecute offenders.

Ms Adeyemo urged residents and community leaders to report illegal borehole drilling and unauthorised groundwater extraction.

Complaints can be made through LASWARCO’s hotline on 0816 878 2223 or at Block 19, third floor, Lagos State Secretariat, Alausa, Ikeja.

World.title: There is no other Stella for Ebola, By Azu Ishiekwene
World.content:
The most expensive thing in Nigeria is not petrol, not food or medicines, not even cement. It is memory loss – an epidemic that has obviously been escalated by screen addiction from its initial default mode of poor record-keeping and absence of institutional diligence.

Nigeria has met Ebola again. Not with the terror of 2014 – which has all but been forgotten – when a Liberian-American named Patrick Sawyer walked into Lagos carrying a virus and a stubborn disregard for other people’s lives.

This time, it’s with a quieter, more bureaucratic alarm – an imported case in Abuja, not from the West but from the east coast of Africa. A 42-year-old woman reportedly arrived from Uganda, developed symptoms four days later, sought care at a private hospital, and tested positive for the Bundibugyo (Ugandan) strain on 20 October.

Ebola, this Time

The good news is that the patient has been evacuated, is in isolation and is receiving care. The bad news is that Nigerians have a special talent for treating preparedness like aso-ebi: impressive on D-day and impossible to find at the next occasion.

Twelve years ago, Ebola taught Nigeria a lesson written in the blood of health workers. It also gave us Dr. Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, the physician whose refusal to let a highly infectious patient leave helped stop an epidemic before it became a national catastrophe. She paid with her life. Nigeria does not need another such invoice.

The current case reads like a travel itinerary. According to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), the patient returned to Abuja from Uganda through Addis Ababa on 3 October. She developed symptoms on 7 October, was admitted to a private health facility on 11 October, and the NCDC was notified on 19 October. Laboratory confirmation came on 20 October.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Follow the Timeline

That timeline deserves attention. There were 17 days between the index case arriving in Abuja and confirmation, and 12 days between symptom onset and notification. In infectious-disease terms, that is not a gap. It is a corridor.

Ebola is not malaria. It does not announce itself with a neon sign. Early symptoms such as fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, and sore throat can masquerade as ordinary ailments that Nigerians treat with paracetamol, prayer, pepper soup, and the national motto: “It is well.”

By 25 October, the NCDC said 53 contacts had been identified and were being monitored. On 26 October, the patient and her husband were medically evacuated to Switzerland, where she is receiving specialised care.

Once Upon a Sawyer

On 20 July, 2014, Sawyer, a Liberian government official, flew from Monrovia to Lagos via Lomé. He was infected with the Zaire strain of Ebola, the deadliest of the species. He collapsed at the airport and was taken to First Consultants Medical Centre in Obalende, where Dr Adadevoh and some of her colleagues took the bullet that could have turned Lagos into an Ebola graveyard.

Sawyer, by several accounts, wanted to leave the hospital. He reportedly resisted isolation. In a country where “the customer is always right” has been elevated to a theology, Adadevoh did something – she disagreed with the customer.

She and her team kept him in the hospital, alerted the authorities, and began the difficult work of containment. Sawyer died on 24 July, 2014. Adadevoh tested positive for the virus on 4 August, while caring for him and died on 19 August, 2014, aged 57.

The Toll

Nigeria eventually recorded 20 Ebola cases and eight deaths in that outbreak. It was declared Ebola-free on 20 October, 2014, barely three months after Sawyer’s arrival. The world called it a success. Nigerians called it a miracle. Both descriptions were true, but neither should obscure the cost: eight people died, including heroic health workers, because one man’s illness met one doctor’s courage.

There is a temptation to reduce Adadevoh’s story to inspiration. Nigerians love inspiration; it is cheaper than infrastructure.

But inspiration is not a substitute for systems. Adadevoh’s heroism was effective because it was eventually supported by contact tracing, laboratory capacity, isolation, communication, and coordination.

The Ebola Emergency Operations Centre, established during that response, became a model praised internationally. It showed that Nigeria could organise when it chose to. Nigeria showed that capacity again with COVID-19 when even first-world countries were confounded.

Forgetfulness Meets Tragedy

That is where forgetfulness meets tragedy. Nigeria does not lack competence. It lacks consistency. We can mobilise brilliantly for a crisis, then dismantle the machinery once the cameras leave. We build emergency operations centres with the urgency of a man whose house is on fire, only to let them gather dust until the next fire.

The 2026 case is a test of institutional memory. Do we still have the laboratories, the trained personnel, the isolation capacity, the surveillance network, the community trust and the political will that carried us through 2014 and COVID-19?

The fact that the NCDC was notified on 19 October, eight days after admission, suggests the system eventually worked. Every day of delay expands the contact list, deepens anxiety and increases the burden on already stretched health workers.

What’s Different?

In 2014, Nigerians received text messages recommending bathing with salt water at dawn. Grown men and women, including some who could operate complex businesses and quote economic statistics, obediently scrubbed themselves with salt. It did not kill Ebola. It did, however, reportedly cause injuries and deaths from excessive salt consumption.

The lesson was simple: panic is also a public-health hazard. Fear makes people hide symptoms, avoid hospitals, blame outsiders and embrace dangerous remedies.

If Dr Adadevoh could speak today, she would probably not ask for statues. She would ask practical questions: Where are the isolation beds, gloves, gowns, face shields? Are oxygen supplies available, not “available on request,” which in Nigerian English means unavailable? Are health workers trained and insured? Is there a functioning referral system from private clinics to public isolation centres? Are contact tracers properly equipped? Is there a single, credible source of information rather than twelve competing WhatsApp broadcasts?

Emergency Love

Nigeria’s political class loves emergencies. An emergency provides photo-ops, special committees, presidential directives and the dizzying grammar of “stakeholders.” One more thing: emergencies are also pipelines for big money, and cash out. Prevention, by contrast, is boring. It involves maintenance, training, data, procurement and accountability.

Perhaps it is instructive that Ebola has visited Nigeria in campaign season, when politicians remember that power resides with voters and move from town to city to village telling deadly lies like the Ebola virus. It will be easier to trace political lies in this season, when politicians are at their mobile best, than to trace a virus.

In Memory of Adadevoh

But the truest memorial to Adadevoh is not a plaque. It is a health system in which no doctor has to choose between personal safety and public duty. It is a country where a suspected case is reported within hours, not days. It is an isolation centre that works before the emergency, not one hastily converted from a conference hall after the first alarm.

Adadevoh stepped on a virus on our behalf. Twelve years later, Ebola has returned with a different strain, a different city and a different patient. The virus has changed its address. The question is whether Nigeria has changed its habits.

Azu Ishiekwene is Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book,Writing for Media and Monetising It.

World.title: ‎NDE targets job growth with five-year plan, revamp of 87 training centres
World.content:
‎

‎…ILO backs modern employment service, stronger labour market data to improve job opportunities

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎ABUJA –The National Directorate of Employment (NDE) has launched a five-year strategic plan aimed at expanding job creation and upgrading its 87 Skills Training Centres, many of which need rehabilitation, modern equipment, or full renovation to meet present-day training requirements.

‎

‎The 2027–2031 plan also aims to enhance employment services, strengthen labour-market information systems, and better align vocational training with industry needs, as the Directorate works to boost job creation and promote sustainable livelihoods throughout Nigeria.

‎

‎Speaking at the unveiling ceremony in Abuja, Thursday, NDE Director-General Silas Agara said the strategy would equip the agency to address shifting labour-market needs through coordinated, evidence-based and results-oriented interventions.

‎

‎He said the plan would give the Directorate’s departments, state offices, and programme delivery structures a shared direction, focusing on demand-driven skills development, entrepreneurship, enterprise growth, strategic partnerships, and inclusive employment.

‎

‎According to him: “The NDE is not merely unveiling a policy document; but setting out a clear strategic direction for the next five years, reaffirming our institutional purpose and strengthening our commitment to creating employment opportunities, developing skills, promoting entrepreneurship and improving the livelihoods of Nigerians.”

‎

‎Speaking on the condition of the agency’s training infrastructure, the Director-General revealed that the NDE operates 87 Skills Training Centres, as well as Agricultural Training Centres and Common Facility Centres. He explained that many of these facilities require varying degrees of retooling, upgrading, rehabilitation, or complete overhaul.

‎

‎He said: “We are committed to modernising these facilities and harmonising our training curricula to ensure uniform standards and alignment with industry needs.”

‎Agara, who was a former deputy governor of Nasarawa state, however, acknowledged that modernising the facilities and improving the quality of training would require sustained support from the Federal Government, development partners and the private sector.

‎

‎He said the Directorate would also strengthen collaboration with employers and industry partners, improve data-driven decision-making and provide more effective post-training support to help beneficiaries secure employment, establish viable businesses and sustain their livelihoods.

‎

‎The NDE boss stressed that employment interventions must respond to the changing nature of work, shaped by technological advancement, emerging industries, demographic pressures and evolving business models.

‎

‎He said the plan would guide resource allocation, performance assessment and programme monitoring, adding that its priorities must be integrated into the Directorate’s annual work plans and budgets to ensure accountability.

‎

‎”The real test of this Plan begins after its launch,” Agara said, emphasising that implementation would require clear responsibilities, adequate resources, measurable targets and effective monitoring mechanisms.

‎

‎In her remarks, the Director of the International Labour Organization (ILO) Country Office for Nigeria, Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone and the Liaison Office for ECOWAS, Vanessa Phala, highlighted the importance of modern employment services and improved labour-market information in translating skills development into better job opportunities.

‎

‎She said the plan’s proposed establishment of a modern Public Employment Service, alongside stronger labour-market information systems and institutional capacity, could improve the connection between job seekers, employers and available economic opportunities.

‎

‎”The planned establishment of a modern Public Employment Service, enhanced labour market information systems, and stronger organisational capacities will not only improve service delivery but also enable more responsive, evidence-based support for job seekers, entrepreneurs, and employers alike,” Phala said.

‎

‎She explained that a modern employment service and reliable labour-market information could help the NDE make better-informed decisions, improve support for job seekers and entrepreneurs, and ensure that employment interventions responded more closely to employers’ needs.

‎

‎Phala described the strategic plan as timely, given the effects of technological change, demographic transitions and evolving skills requirements on Nigeria’s labour market.

‎

‎She also said the plan was well positioned to support the implementation of the National Employment Policy (NEP) 2025 and advance the country’s efforts to promote productive employment and decent work.

‎

‎The ILO director disclosed that the organisation supported the development of the plan through the Strengthening Employment and Employability Systems in Nigeria (SEESIN) project, implemented through the GIZ-ILO collaboration under the Skills Development for Youth Employment Programme (SKYE II).

‎

‎According to her, the process involved consultations with NDE management and staff and a broad range of stakeholders, whose contributions helped identify institutional priorities and strengthen the plan’s relevance to Nigeria’s employment challenges.

‎

‎However, Phala cautioned that achieving the plan’s objectives would require clear institutional leadership, adequate resources, effective partnerships and regular assessment of results.

‎

‎She urged the NDE to assign clear responsibilities for each priority area and called on government institutions, employers’ and workers’ organisations and development partners to align their support with the plan’s objectives.

‎

‎She also emphasised the importance of using results-based management and monitoring, evaluation and learning mechanisms to track progress and strengthen accountability throughout the implementation period.

‎

‎The ILO reaffirmed its commitment to working with the Nigerian government and social partners to translate national employment policies and related frameworks into practical improvements in employment opportunities and livelihoods.

‎

‎Agara, in turn, expressed appreciation to the governments of Germany and Switzerland, the ILO and other development partners for supporting the development of the plan through the GIZ-implemented SKYE II programme.

‎

‎He also acknowledged the contributions of the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment, organised labour, employers’ organisations, civil society organisations and other stakeholders who participated in the consultations and validation process.

‎

World.title: Tinubu defends borrowing plans, says investments ‘ll expand opportunities for future generations
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎ABUJA —PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has responded to criticism, especially from opposition leaders, over new loans the country has accessed from international institutions and banks.

‎

‎In an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” to be published on Nigerian news platforms, President Tinubu wrote: “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind.”

‎

‎He identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and the modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity.

‎

‎The President said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce logistics costs, unlock agricultural and industrial potential and attract private investment.

‎

‎The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to cut logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent. It could add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s GDP through expanded trade, tourism, and industrial activity.

‎

‎The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services.

‎

‎According to him: “We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.”

‎

‎He said the administration’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 would require sustained infrastructure investment to support higher productivity, industrialisation and trade.

‎

‎“We cannot build a USD 1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” Tinubu said.

‎

‎He wrote that improving economic indicators and growing international investor confidence are creating opportunities for Nigeria to attract long-term investment and expand critical infrastructure.

‎

‎The President said the economic reforms his administration introduced in May 2023 helped restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen public finances, and improve the country’s standing in international financial markets.

‎

‎He said a $1 trillion economy would not emerge by declaration alone but must be built through sustained investment, higher productivity, industrialisation, and trade, stressing that infrastructure development would be critical to achieving the target by 2030.

‎

‎In an article titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier.

‎

‎He also said gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 billion in net reserves, while the tax-to-GDP ratio increased to 12.5 per cent from seven per cent.

‎

‎Tinubu said real Gross Domestic Product growth reached 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier.

‎

‎The President attributed the improvements to measures including petrol subsidy removal, exchange rate unification, tax reforms and coordinated efforts to tackle inflation.

‎

‎“The decisions taken since 2023 were difficult but necessary,” he said, referring to the reforms.

‎

‎Tinubu said the gains have strengthened Nigeria’s ability to attract investment and finance projects that support long-term economic growth.

‎

‎“Confidence has a price; our cost of borrowing is going down, and the country risk premium has drastically decreased,” he said.

‎

‎The President cited positive assessments by international credit rating agencies as evidence of improved confidence in the economy.

‎

‎

‎“These are not political endorsements; they are independent assessments by global rating agencies, index providers, regulators and investors, recognising stronger external reserves, improved macroeconomic management and greater financial credibility,” Tinubu said.

‎

‎According to the President, the improved standing could help Nigeria attract more institutional investors, secure longer-term financing and reduce borrowing costs.

‎

‎He said the administration was shifting public borrowing away from financing short-term fiscal pressures towards investments that would generate economic returns, create jobs and expand opportunities for future generations.

‎

‎The President said the government was also pursuing longer-term financing arrangements to match the lifespan of infrastructure assets, reduce refinancing pressures and secure more competitive funding for productive investments.

‎

‎President Tinubu said Nigeria must convert renewed international confidence into capital expenditure, completed infrastructure and lasting economic benefits for citizens.

‎

‎He identified five priorities for the next phase of the Federal Executive Council’s economic strategy: food affordability and energy price stability; budget harmonisation and fiscal discipline; completion of high-impact projects and investment in critical infrastructure; an improved economic policy framework and regulatory efficiency; and targeted household support alongside investment in human development.

‎

‎The President stressed that the success of the current administration’s economic schemes would be measured by completed projects, increased investment, employment generation and improved living standards.

‎

‎“Securing financing is not the achievement. Completing the project, delivering value and improving the lives of Nigerians is the achievement,” he said.

‎

‎He added that the nation’s economic ambition must be supported by responsible borrowing and investments that create lasting opportunities for future generations.

World.title: Osimhen welcomes second child with Cameroonian-German girlfriend
World.content:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and his girlfriend, Stefanie Ladewig, have welcomed their second child, a baby girl named Liora Audrey.

Galatasaray, the Turkish club where Osimhen plays, announced the arrival of the couple’s daughter in a social media post on Thursday.

“Our Football A Team player Victor Osimhen and Stefanie have welcomed a baby girl into the world.

“We congratulate the couple Victor and Stefanie; we wish their newborn baby Liora Audrey a long, healthy, and happy life!” the post read.

The couple’s first daughter, Hailey, was born in October 2022.

Ladewig, a Cameroonian-German fashion model and social media influencer, reportedly began dating Osimhen in 2019 when the Nigerian forward was playing for German Bundesliga side Wolfsburg.

Earlier this month, reports emerged that Ladewig had been involved in a road accident while heavily pregnant. Turkish media reported that she escaped unhurt in the crash, which involved three vehicles.

Meanwhile, Osimhen is expected to feature for Galatasaray in their league fixture against T. Konyaspor on Friday, having been included in the squad for the match.

The 27-year-old forward was in impressive form on Monday, scoring twice to help Galatasaray defeat their fierce Istanbul rivals, Fenerbahce, in the city derby.

Galatasaray currently lead the league standings after nine matches, while Osimhen has scored eight goals, placing him among the competition’s joint-top scorers.

World.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
World.content:
INEC Chair, Joash Amupitan

By Omeiza Ajayi

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28.

Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night.

According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states.

He said, “The complaints concerned the omission of certain political parties, the wrongful inclusion of candidates of political parties whose names were not contained in the membership registers submitted by their political parties, and instances of alleged multiple nominations.”

Haruna said the commission examined the complaints against its records and the law.

“Following a review of the complaints, relevant records and applicable legal provisions, the Commission found merit in some representations and approved the inclusion of affected candidates and their political parties, while complaints found to be without merit were declined.

“In addition, some names that were wrongfully published in the final list were removed after verifying that their names were not on the register.

“The Commission also approved the removal of candidates whose nominations were found to be inconsistent with the applicable legal requirements,” the statement said.

Although INEC did not name any candidate or state, a source had earlier revealed that the commission’s meeting on Thursday to review complaints from parties and candidates left out of the lists had cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections, subject to the outcome of pending court cases.

The source also said the petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list, did not succeed.

“Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP governorship candidate in Gombe State.

“He did not succeed,” the source said when asked about Adebutu.

On the State Houses of Assembly, the commission said the decisions affecting candidates sponsored by political parties “were informed by specific complaints received and determined in accordance with the law and the Commission’s established criteria.”

For those elections, INEC received 61 petitions from 11 political parties across 11 states. Twenty-five succeeded, while 36 failed.

The commission said the affected candidates, political parties and states “will be reflected in the updated list on the Commission’s website.”

“Once again, the Commission assures the public of its commitment to transparency and the credibility of the electoral process,” the statement said.

World.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 to reach League Cup quarter-finals
World.content:
Everton swept into the League Cup quarter-finals with a 3-1 win against Newcastle on Thursday as they booked a clash against giant-killers Fleetwood.

David Moyes’s side took the lead through James Garner’s first-half goal at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Hayden Hackney doubled the lead with his first goal since his close-season move from Middlesbrough.

Everton striker Thierno Barry netted in the second half and Dan Burn’s reply for Newcastle came far too late to stop the Toffees ending their three-match winless run.

Chasing their first League Cup final appearance in 43 years, Everton will travel to fourth-tier minnows Fleetwood in the week commencing December 14.

The ‘Cod Army’ caused one of the biggest shocks in League Cup history on Tuesday when they beat Premier League champions Arsenal in a penalty shoot-out after a 1-1 draw at Highbury.

Everton have never won the League Cup, losing their two final appearances in 1977 and 1984.

Everton fans do not need reminding that it is 31 years since the club won the FA Cup in their most recent trophy triumph.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, a noted Everton fan, is old enough to remember that success and he was cheering from the stands as Moyes’s men made light work of their last-16 tie.

Newcastle will have the chance for revenge when the sides meet again in the Premier League at St James’ Park on Monday.

Everton dropped a pre-match bombshell, saying Jack Grealish was unavailable for selection “due to a breach of club discipline”.

Grealish, beset by criticism of his behaviour off the pitch, was reported to have taken an unauthorised absence from training.

But the on-loan Manchester City winger’s absence was no problem for his team-mates.

– Everton hit their stride –

Newcastle tested Jordan Pickford early on when Joe Willock’s low drive was palmed away by the Everton goalkeeper, who repelled Fabian Schar’s long-range strike moments later.

Garner steadied Everton’s nerves with a clinical opener in the 34th minute.

Hackney teed up Garner just inside the area and the midfielder stretched to guide a fine finish into the far corner for his first goal since January.

Everton had hit their stride and Hackney struck on the stroke of half-time.

At the climax of a blistering Everton counter-attack, Barry hooked a cross into the six-yard box and Hackney timed his run perfectly to volley past Lukas Hornicek.

Frustrated Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Joelinton, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa at the interval.

Wissa had an immediate chance after sprinting onto Willock’s pass, but he misjudged the high bounce and ended up heading straight at Pickford.

It was a costly miss as Barry put the result beyond doubt in the 69th minute.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall provided the cross and Barry lashed home from close range for his seventh goal this season.

Burn scored with a header from Willock’s 88th-minute cross, sparking a brawl between several players.

But Newcastle’s brief show of defiance was too little, too late as Everton moved a step closer to Wembley.

AFP

World.title: 2027: Utomi, Ohaa, Yesufu urge Nigerians to mobilise support for Obi
World.content:
Peter Obi

Chieftains of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have urged Nigerians to mobilise grassroots support for the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, come 2027.

The party chieftains, including a political economist, Prof Pat Utomi, Enugu State NDC governorship candidate, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa and human rights activist, Aisha Yesufu, made the call on Thursday during the Obi-Kwankwaso Town Hall Meeting held in Enugu.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Obi, his running mate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, and other NDC stakeholders attended the meeting, which attracted a large crowd of supporters.

Addressing the crowd, Utomi expressed confidence that the Obi-Kwankwaso presidential ticket would provide the leadership needed to address Nigeria’s economic, political and security challenges.

He lamented that Nigeria’s potential to become one of the greatest countries in the world had been undermined by corruption, criminality and disunity.

According to him, the time has come for Nigerians to unite and work towards achieving meaningful political change.

“We have done our research, and I know that a combination of Peter Gregory Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso will deliver Nigeria,” he said.

Utomi urged Nigerians to turn out massively during the elections, vote for their preferred candidates and defend their votes through lawful means.

In his remarks, Ohaa, the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, described the Obi-Kwankwaso political alliance as a historic opportunity to strengthen national unity and promote inclusive governance.

He said the partnership represented the possibility of building political bridges across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones.

According to him, the alliance is reminiscent of the historic political understanding between the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe and Sir Ahmadu Bello during Nigeria’s early political development.

“My message today is simple: we must seize this opportunity and work with our brothers and sisters across the South-South, South-West, North-East, North-West and North-Central to secure an NDC president in 2027,” he said.

Ohaa explained that the campaign was not merely about producing a president of Igbo extraction but about establishing a government committed to justice, accountability, security and prosperity for all Nigerians.

He expressed confidence that NDC candidates in Enugu State were prepared to earn the trust of voters and secure victory in the elections.

Yesufu, a human rights activist, urged Nigerians to take ownership of the 2027 elections by mobilising voters and actively participating in the democratic process.

She said the election was not merely about Obi’s presidential ambition but about the collective responsibility of Nigerians to rescue the country from its numerous challenges.

According to her, the election is not about Obi but about every one of us, as the mistake we made in 1999 must be corrected.

“The class of 1999 has destroyed this country. The class of 2027 must fix this country.

“We must take this election as our own election. Mr Peter Obi and his running mate have one business, and that is to be on the ballot paper.You and I must do the remaining work to ensure victory,” she said.

Yesufu challenged every supporter to mobilise at least 20 eligible voters for Obi, stressing that political change required collective action rather than depending solely on candidates.

The activist also urged Nigerians to demonstrate courage and determination in protecting their votes during the elections, saying that Nigerians must reject political intimidation and insist on credible elections that reflect the will of the people.

Earlier, the NDC Chairman in Enugu State, Mr Ibuchukwu Obetta, welcomed Obi, Kwankwaso and other party leaders to the state, describing their visit as a significant moment in the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections.

Obetta said the visit had renewed the confidence of party members and strengthened their determination to work for a Nigeria founded on integrity, accountability, competence, justice and inclusive development.

(NAN)

World.title: I’ll work closely with Kwankwaso if elected, Obi reassures
World.content:
The NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, (BBC)

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has reiterated willingness to work closely with his vice-presidential candidate, Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso, to move the country forward.

Obi gave the assurance on Thursday during a town hall meeting in Enugu, where he engaged supporters and stakeholders on the country’s challenges and his vision for national development.

The former Anambra State governor said they would work together to tackle insecurity and restore safety across Nigeria if elected president in 2027.

He said that securing lives and property would be a priority of his administration, promising to confront the security challenges threatening communities and livelihoods across the country.

The presidential candidate regretted that the current administration had failed to protect the lives and property of Nigerians, which he maintained was the primary responsibility.

Obi assured voters in the South East to vote for him because of his competence and ability to tackle challenges facing the nation.

He challenged other presidential candidates to meet and discuss their plans, and warned the people not to be deceived by rhetoric and propaganda.

On education, Obi said he would declare a state of emergency on education to enable his administration to tackle the issue of out-of-school children head-on, hinting that Nigerian children deserved quality education.

In his remarks, the vice-presidential candidate of NDC, Kwankwaso, advised that nobody should be deceived by ethnicity, saying, “It’s obvious that Nigerians are going through numerous difficulties”.

Kwankwaso lamented that people were facing challenges like insecurity, unemployment, poverty, hunger and so many other challenges.

He explained that the only solution to achieve a new Nigeria was unity, diligence, perseverance and willingness.

He urged Nigerians to come out en masse to cast, protect and follow up on their votes until results were announced, noting that it was not a one-man show but a collective responsibility.

Also, Sen Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly, described Obi and his running mate, Kwankwaso, as the “best presidential ticket” to lead Nigeria.

Umeh expressed confidence that the South-East would rally behind Obi in the 2027 presidential election, urging the people to remain resolute and resist attempts to intimidate or discourage them from pursuing their political choice.

He also commended the resilience of supporters who, according to him, ensured that the meeting held despite reported attempts to frustrate the gathering.

The senator further praised Kwankwaso for his efforts to build support in Northern Nigeria, expressing optimism that the Obi-led ticket could attract votes across the country.

Umeh urged the people of the South-East to use their votes to make a strong political statement in 2027, declaring his support for Obi’s presidential ambition and calling on the region to unite behind the project.

(NAN)

World.title: Inter, AC Milan unveil new stadium plans to replace San Siro
World.content:
San Siro

Inter and AC Milan unveiled their new “Generali Stadium” Thursday, which will replace the iconic San Siro stadium from the 2031/32 season.

It will be shaped “low in the body, and it rises up at either end” behind the goals, architect Norman Foster said during a press conference in Milan.

The design aims to bring spectators as close to the pitch as possible, with the stands behind the goals set at a steep 37-degree incline, said David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project.

“The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that the San Siro is a feeling,” he said.

“It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling, and everything that we needed to do here was to carry it into the (new) building”.

Manica said the design team “started with proximity”.

“We brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass,” he said.

They also paid great attention to acoustics: the roof covers the stands, leaving only the pitch exposed, and is designed to “amplify the roar” of the fans, Manica said.

“This building is steeper than many other new buildings are built today, and that’s intentional, because it allows us to bring those seats up and over the field as much as possible, and create that sense of intimacy and atmosphere,” he said.

The stadium, sponsored by the Italian insurance giant Generali, will also be capable of hosting American football games, rugby matches and concerts.

“I want the crowd to come to the new stadium and to feel that excitement that they felt before, and to feel the building, living and breathing with them as it does currently,” Manica said.

AC Milan and Inter paid 197 million euros ($219 million) to acquire the current stadium and its adjacent parking areas, where they intend to build their new, shared home.

The project for the new San Siro — which will have a capacity of 71,500 seats, compared to the current 75,000 — will cost the two clubs 1.2 billion euros.

Construction is set to begin in 2028.

Foster and Manica previously worked together on London’s Wembley Stadium.

Milan’s current stadium — one of the most iconic in European football and often likened to a “concrete cathedral” — is the largest in Italy.

But the venue, which opened in 1926, no longer meets the needs of spectators or the clubs, despite undergoing several renovations over the decades.

San Siro, also known as the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium, will be largely demolished once construction work on the new stadium nears completion.

World.title: Shipping Experts Berate Banks, NIMASA Over Slow Pace of Cabotage Vessel Financing Disbursements
World.content:
Eromosele Abiodun

Shipping experts yesterday in Lagos blamed the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) poor regulatory framework and banks stringent conditions for the persistent delays in the cabotage vessel financing fund disbursements.

The experts, who spoke at the annual summit of the Shipping Correspondents Association of Nigeria (SCAN), said that regulatory uncertainty continues to drive up investment costs, severely discouraging long-term financial commitments needed to build a robust domestic maritime fleet.

The experts highlighted that Nigeria’s maritime sector urgently requires a stable and transparent operational framework to thrive.

A Maritime Lawyer, Founding Partner, AOL, and former President, Nigeria Bar Association, Dr Olisa Agbakoba, said regulatory uncertainty increases investment costs and discourages long-term financing.

To restore investor confidence and unlock critical funding, Agbakoba called for consistent enforcement of maritime regulations, transparent administrative procedures, clearly defined institutional responsibilities, and a predictable system for administering applicable waivers.

Agbakoba said that without proactive intervention from the agency, indigenous operators will continue to lose lucrative opportunities in coastal trade to foreign competitors.

He emphasised the need for effective coordination between NIMASA and key government bodies, including the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), and the Nigerian Ports Economic Regulatory Agency (NPERA).

He noted that only an aligned, transparent regulatory environment can ensure timely disbursements and empower local shipowners to drive the nation’s maritime economy.

Also, he stated that, “Banks and institutional investors must become active partners in developing Nigeria’s National Fleet. This requires specialized maritime credit expertise, reliable vessel valuations, technical assessments, and sound legal advice on ship mortgages, charter contracts, insurance, and cross-border enforcement.

“Financing should be tailored to each vessel’s commercial circumstances. A vessel supported by a credible long-term charter contract carries a different risk profile from one dependent on uncertain spot-market earnings.

“Commercial banks, development finance institutions, insurers, private investors, and export credit agencies should explore appropriate combinations of debt, equity, leasing, guarantees, and other financing arrangements,” he stated.

According to Agbakoba, the Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund (CVFF) remains an important instrument for supporting indigenous vessel ownership, but fleet development cannot depend principally on public financing. \He added that public financing should support viable projects and mobilize private capital, not substitute for a functioning commercial shipping market.

“The Fund should complement commercial bank lending, development finance, private investment, and cargo-backed financing. Its administration requires transparent eligibility criteria, rigorous credit assessment, appropriate collateral, clear risk allocation, effective monitoring, and recovery arrangements.

“The focus must shift from simply seeking money to acquire vessels towards developing viable transactions that connect cargo demand, suitable vessels, credible operators, and willing financiers,” he stated.

“Without dependable cargo, shipowners will struggle to attract capital. Without credible operators and effective security, lenders will hesitate. Without regulatory certainty, investors may decline otherwise viable opportunities.

“We must therefore move beyond asking, “Where will the money to acquire Nigerian vessels come from?” and ask a more fundamental question: “Where is the cargo and commercial opportunity that will make Nigerian vessels financeable?” he stated.

Speaking, former Director-General of the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), Temisan Omatseye, presented a critical appraisal of local commercial banks and existing fund structures, arguing that current financing models fall short of empowering local operators to compete globally.

“There is money available for this, and I keep telling people that we can never be competitive in our shipping industry because of what? Sorry, bankers may not like this. The banks in Nigeria do not have the capacity to finance shipping. One LNG tanker alone is about $250 million. Repayment cannot be less than 15 years. I’m sorry to say this again, our banks are just traders looking for short-term loans,” he stated.

Commending SCAN for bringing critical issues to the fore, the United Bank for Africa (UBA), Regional Manager, Apapa, Nelson Edoye, called for structured partnerships across sectors.

“The gap requires deliberate partnership within the financial sector and the maritime stakeholders,” Edoye noted.

He said: “The maritime sector remains a cornerstone for economic diversification, job creation and national prosperity. Yet, indigenous shipowners continue to face the twin challenges of access to patient capital and regulatory complexities. Bridging this gap requires deliberate partnership between the financial sector, regulators, and industry stakeholders.

“At UBA, with our presence in 20 African countries and global operations, we understand the capital-intensive nature of shipping and the need for innovative, de-risked financing structures. We remain committed to supporting indigenous participation in the maritime value chain through tailored financing solutions, trade facilitation, and advisory services that unlock growth and enhance competitiveness,” he stated

World.title: UBA Breaks New Ground with Google Pay for Visa, Mastercard Users
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has set new standards in digital banking by being the first to enable Google Pay for eligible Visa and Mastercard users, reinforcing its commitment towards delivering innovative, secure and convenient payment solutions.

With this development, eligible customers can now make fast and convenient digital payments using compatible devices, further enhancing their banking experience and expanding access to modern payment technologies.

UBA’s Directorate Head, Cards, Orry Seem, highlighted the importance of making everyday banking and payments simpler for customers.

“Our customers live busy lives, and the way they pay should make those lives easier. For many of them, the phone is the first thing they reach for, so it makes sense for it to become their wallet too,” she said.

She added, “Being the first bank in the country to be enabled on Google Pay reflects our commitment to enabling customers to transact locally and internationally, wherever Google Pay is accepted. At UBA, putting the customer first means bringing the best of global innovation home.”

UBA’s Group Head, Brands, Marketing and Corporate Communications, Alero Ladipo, said the move reflects the Bank’s broader ambition to lead the adoption of innovative digital payment solutions and deliver greater value to customers.

“Digital payment in Nigeria is growing fast, and customers expect more ways to pay. Making Google Pay available to our Visa and Mastercard cardholders gives them a simple, fast option for everyday purchases, backed by the security of their UBA cards,” Ladipo said.

She noted that embracing global payment platforms early gives customers more choice while strengthening UBA’s position as a leader in digital banking across its markets.

World.title: Integrating Nigeria’s Fragmented Transport System
World.content:
Chinedu Eze

Experts have advocated for the integration of Nigeria’s transport system, including road, rail, aviation and maritime, in order to develop policies that will synergize the movement of goods and services across the nation.

The experts who converged last week in Lagos at the second Nigeria Transport Summit with the theme: ‘Navigating Global Disruptions and the Road Ahead: Mobility, Energy and Trade Facilitation for a Resilient Future’, also called for the adoption of multifaceted security apparatus to protect the multi–modal transportation system.

Looking at the critical role the maritime sector plays in the transportation of goods, the Nigerian Ports Economic Regulatory Agency (NPERA) advocated for the use of evidence-based regulation and stakeholder engagement to eliminate avoidable logistics costs, lower the cost of trade, and streamline cargo clearance operations across Nigeria’s ports.

In his presentation at the summit, the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NPERA, Akutah Pius Ukeyima, stated that trade bottlenecks, unpredictable port charges, and fragmented infrastructure continued to harm the country’s commercial competitiveness.

“Through effective stakeholder engagement, appropriate regulatory measures and evidence-based decision-making, NPERA is committed to supporting a port system that reduces avoidable costs, improves operational efficiency, encourages fair competition and strengthens Nigeria’s position as a competitive maritime and trade destination,” Akutah said.

Highlighting the economic impact of logistics challenges, Akutah noted that seamless trade facilitation is indispensable to national growth.

“Delays in cargo clearance, excessive or unpredictable charges, inadequate infrastructure and weak coordination among stakeholders can increase logistics costs and undermine the competitiveness of Nigerian businesses,” he warned.

To address these hurdles, the NPERA chief emphasised that economic regulation must protect the commercial interests of all operators—including importers, exporters, shipping companies, and freight forwarders—while fostering predictable investment conditions.

“Effective economic regulation is essential to ensuring that charges are reasonable, service delivery is efficient, stakeholders are treated fairly and the interests of port users are adequately protected within the applicable regulatory framework,” he explained.

Addressing the systemic challenges beyond maritime gates, Akutah urged federal authorities and private operators to accelerate integration across roads, rail lines, and inland waterways.

“The development of an efficient transport system cannot be achieved through ports and roads alone. It requires effective integration of road, rail, inland waterways and other transport modes to facilitate the seamless movement of cargo from the ports to inland markets and production centres,” Akutah noted.

He added that dry ports and supporting transit infrastructures play a strategic role in expanding access for hinterland businesses, provided connection bottlenecks are resolved.

“We must therefore continue to address bottlenecks affecting rail freight services, road transport costs, cargo documentation, shipping arrangements and the effective utilization of inland transport infrastructure,” he urged.

Looking at insecurity in his presentation at the summit, the Executive Director of Operations and Technical at Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Warredi Enisuoh, called for the integration of security awareness in school curriculum to prepare young Nigerians to protect their society in the face of insecurity ravaging the country.

Enisuoh who is a seasoned airline captain, ship master, and maritime security expert emphasised that criminal elements systematically exploit public unawareness and outdated infrastructure.

Enisuoh warned that the nation can no longer afford a reactive approach to security threats, noting that widespread indifference exposes citizens to preventable dangers.

“When it comes to security, the problem is people have to be aware. It is awareness or unawareness that your assailants take advantage of. If people know that you are aware, it helps douse down the insecurity because those who carry out threats always take advantage of the fact that you are not aware. So awareness is key,” Enisuoh stated.

He stressed that the reality of kidnapping and security risks must be directly countered through early childhood and adolescent education.

“The amount of insecurity that has somehow inflicted this country is not reflected in the day-to-day education of our children in school. We should start teaching insecurity in school now,” Enisuoh asserted.

He further said: “Because those who will be kidnapped tomorrow are free today. Everybody seems to feel it’s not their business or ‘not my portion,’ but the person who was taken yesterday felt the same way. We have to increase our educational syllabus to handle insecurity lectures because this is something that has come to stay.”

Critiquing Nigeria’s current transport and logistics infrastructure, Enisuoh noted that the nation’s sea ports and highways were never structurally designed to withstand or mitigate modern security risks.

Comparing sector performances, he pointed out that Nigeria’s aviation industry has performed remarkably well due to stringent international auditing, perimeter fencing, and strict access controls, adding that the maritime domain has much to learn from airport security frameworks.

The convener of the summit, Mrs. Pearl Ngwama, in her opening speech observed that mounting geopolitical instability, volatile global oil markets, and crippling maritime trade disruptions, were posing immediate threats to Nigeria’s economic survival unless the nation moves aggressively to integrate its fragmented transportation networks.

Ngwama in her speech emphasised that external global shocks are directly exacerbating the logistical challenges of domestic transport costs, squeezing businesses, and fueling consumer inflation across Nigeria.

Highlighting the immediate ripple effects of international crises on Nigerian households, Ngwama pointed to recent data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), showed crude oil prices spiking to $131 per barrel in mid-September 2026 following attacks on international energy infrastructure.

“For the transport industry, the consequences are immediate. Airlines face mounting aviation fuel bills; shipping companies contend with higher vessel operating and insurance costs; road haulage operators experience increased fuel expenses; and businesses must absorb rising logistics costs. Ultimately, these pressures translate into higher passenger fares, more expensive goods, and reduced competitiveness,” Ngwama said.

She further cited UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) and Reuters reports showing that shipping throughput via the Red Sea remains 70 percent below 2023 levels, while the cost of chartering supertankers on key international routes surged to $81 million compared to $9.1 million a year prior.

“Nigeria cannot control global oil prices or determine the outcome of international conflicts. However, we can strengthen our domestic transport infrastructure, improve operational efficiency, and develop policies that reduce the extent to which external shocks undermine our economy,” she said.

Ngwama cautioned that while global disruptions originate abroad, they primarily expose deep-seated structural flaws within Nigeria’s internal logistics architecture. She called for an immediate end to uncoordinated, isolated policy-making across aviation, maritime, rail, road, and inland waterways.

According to her, “Nigeria possesses considerable advantages, yet these advantages will remain underutilized unless our transport modes function as parts of an integrated system. A seaport cannot achieve its full economic potential when cargo evacuation is inefficient. A railway cannot deliver maximum value without effective connections to ports, industrial centers, and road networks.”

She stressed that achieving multimodal integration is crucial if Nigerian businesses hope to capitalize on the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), warning that access to a 1.3-billion-person continental market will yield little if local producers cannot move goods competitively.

Beyond infrastructure, the summit convener identified energy reliability, digital cargo tracking, and regulatory predictability as non-negotiable pillars for building sector resilience.

World.title: FCMB, Mastercard Launch Digital Platform to Expand Financing for Farmers
World.content:
First City Monument Bank (FCMB) and Mastercard have launched AgroPass, a digital platform designed to expand access to finance, markets and agricultural services for smallholder farmers across Nigeria.

The platform, developed by Mastercard, connects farmers with input suppliers, buyers, lenders, agribusinesses, and other participants in the agricultural value chain, aiming to strengthen financial inclusion and improve productivity in one of Nigeria’s most important economic sectors.

Speaking at the launch event in Lagos, Yemisi Edun, Managing Director, FCMB, represented by Obaro Odeghe, Executive Director, Wholesale Banking, said: “Supporting farmers means more than offering credit. It is about building connections to finance, markets, technology, knowledge and opportunity. AgroPass is a platform that empowers farmers to become more productive, resilient and commercially successful. By bridging critical gaps across the value chain, we can help build a more sustainable future for agriculture.”

Edun said FCMB provided more than 364.6 billion naira ($236 million) in financing to Nigeria’s agricultural sector last year and supported more than 196,000 smallholder farmers nationwide. Nearly half of the beneficiaries were women and young people.

Executive Vice President, Growth Segments, Mastercard, Tara Nathan said: “Smallholder farmers are at the heart of food systems, rural livelihoods and economic growth across Africa, yet many remain disconnected from the services and opportunities that can help them thrive. AgroPass is designed to bridge those gaps by connecting farmers to financial services, suppliers, buyers and digital tools that support productivity and resilience. Through our collaboration with FCMB, we are helping create a more connected agricultural ecosystem where farmers can build stronger businesses, participate more fully in the economy and unlock new opportunities for growth.”

World.title: Report: Payments Cost Airlines $24.5bn in 2025
World.content:
Stories by Chinedu Eze

The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has released new data showing that airlines globally incurred $24.5 billion in payment costs to process $1.05 trillion in sales in 2025.

According to the global body, the new data has confirmed the rising cost burden of payment processing in airline ticketing purchase.

The aforementioned figure is a 10.4 per cent increase in total costs compared to 2023 and IATA said this far exceeds the overall growth in travel sales over the same period, which was up 7.7 per cent from $977 billion in 2023.

IATA noted that the average cost per transaction was $5 per passenger. In comparison, the Association forecasts that airlines will make a net profit of $4.50 per passenger in 2026.

Giving further details, IATA’s Interim Director General and CFO, Sandrine Le Borgne, said: “The airline industry is hyper competitive, capital intensive and famously low margin (in profit). In such an environment every cost item needs to be looked at carefully. The fact that payment transaction costs are increasing faster than industry revenues is unsustainable and, despite significant technological advances, highlights the critical need for greater cost efficiency.”

Further analysis of the $24.5 billion cost of payments in 2025 revealed that $20.7 billion (84.5 per cent of the total) was related to payment fees or the direct cost of completing each transaction; $2.9 billion (11.8 per cent of the total) was related to airline operating costs, including various payment systems, delayed cashflow, staff, and compliance; $0.9 billion (3.7 per cent of the total) was lost due to fraud or uncollected sales and Cards accounted for the highest cost per transaction with average payment fees at 2.53 per cent, higher than the estimated overall average of 1.97 per cent. The lowest-cost payment options were at 0.01 per cent.

IATA stated that it is exploring several solutions and guidance that will bring efficiency to payments to airlines including introducing alternative, lower-cost forms of payment for passengers.

It disclosed that the 2025 IATA Global Passenger Survey revealed that 29 per cent of passengers prefer to use a digital wallet and eight per cent prefer a local instant payment solution.

IATA is also looking at IATA Pay and IATA Financial Gateway (IFG), expressing optimism that these will help airlines meet the challenges of changing passenger preferences for payment.

The association explained that IATA Pay, which enables passengers to use local instant payment solutions to purchase travel, has been rolled out in 34 countries with 38 payment schemes. IFG is a platform that allows airlines and travel suppliers to manage, optimize, and control travel industry payments across multiple sales channels in more than 170 countries and using 300-plus payment methods.

“In addition to cost-efficiency, IATA research shows that providing passengers with alternative payment methods could also have a revenue-generating impact. About one in five ancillary purchase attempts are not completed because the initial payment attempt was refused and no other method was offered. Enabling more payment options has the potential to help airlines realize some of this lost revenue,” Le Borgne further said.

World.title: Union Bank’s Ayeni Named Among Nigeria’s Top Marketing Communications Professionals
World.content:
Bukola Ayeni, Team Lead, External Communications at Union Bank of Nigeria Plc, has earned a place among Nigeria’s outstanding young marketing communications professionals following her recognition at the 2026 BrandComm 35 Under 35 Awards.

The honour recognises her contributions to corporate communications, brand development, public relations and reputation management, marking another milestone in a career spanning nearly a decade.

Ayeni has built a strong professional background in integrated marketing communications, business strategy, digital marketing, crisis communication and stakeholder engagement, combining creativity with practical business solutions.

At Union Bank, she has contributed to major communication campaigns, executive visibility, stakeholder relations and initiatives aimed at strengthening the bank’s reputation.

One of her notable contributions was providing communications and public relations support for the bank’s Endless Possibilities campaign, which highlights Union Bank’s commitment to supporting the ambitions of Nigerians.

Speaking at the event, the convener, Joshua Ajayi, emphasised the importance of trust and meaningful relationships between brands and consumers.

“You cannot buy connection with volume alone. You earn it through relevance, honesty and respect,” he said.

The keynote speaker, Dr Victor Gbenga Afolabi, Group Chief Executive Officer of Hazon Holdings and GDM Group, said successful brand building must go beyond advertising and public relations to include quality products, effective service delivery and positive customer experiences.

Before joining Union Bank, Ayeni spent six years at Business School Netherlands (BSN), where she gained experience in brand management, digital marketing and corporate communications. She worked with teams in the Netherlands and South Africa on initiatives covering Europe, Africa and Asia.

During this period, she developed and executed BSN Transformation Moment, a 12-month radio programme on Inspiration FM, Lagos. The 49-episode programme featured business leaders and entrepreneurs who shared insights on business growth and leadership.

World.title: SAHCO Secures Air Algeria Ground Handling Contract for Lagos, Abuja Airports
World.content:
Skyway Aviation Handling Company Plc (SAHCO) has strengthened its dominance in Nigeria’s aviation ground handling sector with the award of the Air Algeria ground handling contract for Lagos and Abuja airports, reinforcing its position as a trusted partner to leading international airlines.

​The company said the contract represented another significant milestone in SAHCO’s growth trajectory, reinforcing the confidence international airlines continue to place in the Company’s operational capabilities, service quality and commitment to global aviation standards.

​Under the agreement, SAHCO will provide full ground handling services to Air Algeria at both the Murtala Muhammed International airport in Lagos and the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja leveraging its highly trained workforce, modern ground support equipment and operational expertise to deliver safe, seamless and efficient services in line with international best practices.

​The partnership further strengthens SAHCO’s growing portfolio of international airline clients and underscores its capacity to deliver consistent, high-quality ground handling services across multiple airport locations in Nigeria.

​Commenting on the development, the Chairman of SAHCO Plc, Barr. Taiwo Afolabi CON expressed delight at the partnership, describing the contract as a testament to the Company’s growing reputation for operational excellence and dependable service delivery.

​He stated: “We are delighted that Air Algérie has chosen SAHCO as its ground handling partner in Lagos and Abuja. This confidence reflects our unwavering commitment to safety, operational efficiency and service excellence. We remain focused on delivering seamless ground handling solutions that meet the expectations of our airline partners and contribute to a superior passenger experience.”

​SAHCO’s extensive operational footprint gives it a distinctive advantage in Nigeria’s aviation ground handling industry. As the only ground handling company with a presence at all commercially operated airports in the country, SAHCO combines nationwide reach with a strong commitment to service consistency, reliability and operational excellence.

​The company’s continued investment in modern ground support equipment, technology and workforce development has further strengthened its capacity to meet the evolving needs of domestic and international airlines. Its equipment strategy also incorporates alternative power sources and environmentally conscious solutions, reinforcing its commitment to more sustainable aviation operations.

​Safety remains central to SAHCO’s operations. The company maintains internationally recognized certifications, including ISAGO, RA3, ISO 900, SON and ISO 27001, demonstrating its commitment to quality management, secure operations and globally accepted aviation standards.

​The Air Algeria contract adds to SAHCO’s growing portfolio of international airline partnerships and reflects the confidence airlines continue to place in its expertise, dependable workforce and customer-focused approach.

World.title: Ex-Nigeria Airways Staff Visits Skypower to Process Severance Benefit
World.content:
The ongoing final severance payment process for the former workers of the defunct Nigeria Airways has attracted a large crowd of the ex-staff and their next-of-kin at the Skypower premises at the Murtala Muhammed Airport (MMA), Lagos.

The process, which is in its last stage, is expected to benefit over 5,000 staff of the defunct Nigeria Airways.

Speaking during the exercise, the Director, Presidential initiative Continuos Audit (PICA) in the Ministry of Finance, Mr. Seldam Dangin, said they were making a huge payment to the former workers, while claims involving deceased workers and their next-of-kin are still undergoing verification.

It was gathered that verification of the next-of-kin of deceased former employees commenced last week across the six geopolitical zones of the country.

Dangin further disclosed that the verification exercise is aimed at establishing the identities and eligibility of the next-of-kin before the processing and payment of the outstanding severance benefits due to them.

He said the exercise is coordinated by the Federal Ministry of Finance as part of efforts to conclude the long-running payment process and ensure that all eligible beneficiaries receive their entitlements.

A beneficiary of the exercise, said that the government was committed to ensuring that both surviving former employees and the rightful next-of-kin of deceased beneficiaries were covered, subject to the completion of the required verification and documentation.

In response to a question, Dangin further said that the Ministry of Finance, through this action, was determined to conduct the exercise in a transparent, orderly, and accountable manner to facilitate the successful conclusion of the final payment process.

The commencement of the verification exercise across the six geopolitical zones is expected to help establish the claims of beneficiaries who could not receive their entitlements before the death of the former employees.

He said: “As you can see, the final process has commenced. In the Lagos zone alone, we have thousands of the former workers who have stormed the Skypower premises for verification of their documents. Things are going on peacefully.”

“The Ministry of Finance is doing the due diligence to ensure that everyone is captured in this last exercise. We are very hopeful that the process will end well,” he added.

World.title: Ngizwe Mchunu accused of assaulting baby mama

World.title: Actress Carina Nel on ‘paralysing’ breast cancer diagnosis
World.content:
Carina Nel has opened up about hr breast cancer diagnosis. Images via YouTube screenshot

Former 7de Laan actress Carina Nel – known for playing medical doctor Alexa Welman – has opened up about receiving a “paralysing” breast cancer diagnosis following a routine check-up.

The mother-of-two, who shared her journey during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, is currently undergoing chemotherapy treatment and is in good spirits.

CARINA NEL ON BREAST CANCER DIAGNOSIS

Speaking to SABC’s Expresso show, Carina Nel revealed that a routine check-up in April, after suffering from exhaustion, set off alarm bells.



Five days later, she had been formally diagnosed with breast cancer.

Carina shared that she had no history of breast cancer in her family, and at 38 years old, she was shocked at her diagnosis.

“The five days before I received my daignosis was probably the worst days in this whole journey. It was filled with paralysing fear, where you can’t think, you can’t breathe, you can’t move…

“No one can really understand what it feels like, or what you’re going through until you’re in that situation”.

Carina added that her Christian faith had encouraged her to keep going, and fighting.

She continued: “I remember being overwhelmed with this calmness”.



‘GO GET IT CHECKED’

Like Carina Nel, rugby referee Aimee Barrett-Theron has also gone public with her battle with breast cancer.

The 39-year-old – a qualified biokineticist specialising in sports performance and rehabilitation – shared her diagnosis in July, stating that she would step away from the pitch to undergo treatment.

She has used her platform to encourage women to get screened for breast cancer.

She said in a video interview with the URC: “Early detection is so important when it comes to breast cancer. I was very lucky to find mine in the early stages. I think it literally saved my very active career and potentially my life.

“I chose to share it publicly, and what I found is a lot of people have said that they’re guilty of not doing the self-checks and not going for their scans.

“And, you know, life is busy or they’re worried about the outcome.

“But hopefully, by standing up for this and raising a bit of awareness around it, people are more proactive, and they take action to look after themselves.”

“What I want to stress is we know our bodies best. And if something doesn’t feel right, please go get it checked. It could literally have a massive impact on your treatment plan as well as your future.”

World.title: ‘That increase is more realistic’: South Africans back the proposed SASSA old-age grant amount
World.content:
Not every South African is holding out for a dramatic jump in the SASSA old-age grant. Some say the amount currently on the table is the one most likely to happen.

The comments followed The South African’s report on a push for Parliament to support raising the Older Persons Grant to R3 000 a month.

‘More realistic’

On The South African’s Facebook page, Detlef Weber said the proposed figure strikes the right balance. “That increase is more realistic…” he wrote.



His comment drew a reply and several reactions, with some users agreeing that a smaller, achievable increase is better than a bigger promise that never arrives.

Weber’s view stands apart from many others in the thread, where commenters called for the SASSA old-age grant to rise to R5 000, R6 000, or tomatch the national minimum wage.

Every rand counts in the grant

Tania Steenkamp shared a similar outlook. “R600 is better than nothing. Would be a great addition,” she wrote.



For pensioners who rely on the grant alone, an extra few hundred rand each month can cover a grocery top-up, transport to a clinic or part of a municipal bill.

Supporters of a moderate increase argue that government is more likely to approve an amount that fits within existing budget pressures, rather than a figure that would require major cuts elsewhere.

Weighing ambition against affordability

The debate highlights a tension many grant recipients face. On one side are those who say the grant has never matched the true cost of living. On the other are those who fear pushing for too much could stall any progress at all.



Both groups agree on one thing: the current grant is under strain as food and electricity prices continue to rise.

What happens next

The proposed increase has not been approved. Any change to grant amounts must be announced by the Minister of Finance, usually in the Budget Speech each February, with new amounts taking effect from April.

Until then, grant recipients will continue to receive their monthly payments at current rates and should check official SASSA channels for confirmed updates.

World.title: ‘Not everyone is eligible’: Refugee programme sparks backlash
World.content:
The US Embassy has clarified expectations about the refugee resettlement programme. Image via Canva

The US Embassy’s statement that “not everyone is eligible” for the refugee programme, open to racial minorities like white Afrikaner farmers, has been met with backlash from applicants.

This comes amid reports that hundreds of South Africans have been rejected for various reasons.

It also follows news that one refugee – Arno Venter – who resettled in Ohio with his family, was arrested on over 11 charges of child porn distribution.



US EMBASSY: ‘NOT EVERYONE IS ELIGIBLE FOR REFUGEE PROGRAMME’

In a statement shared on their X account, the US Embassy set the record straight regarding expectations for the refugee programme.

It shared: “Not everyone seeking refugee resettlement in the United States is eligible.

“U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has informed some USRAP applicants in South Africa that their cases are ineligible for continued processing, meaning their applications will not move forward.



“USCIS reviews each application on a case-by-case basis to determine whether applicants meet all requirements under U.S. law.

🇺🇸 𝐀𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐥𝐥 𝐔𝐒𝐑𝐀𝐏 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐝?



Not everyone seeking refugee resettlement in the United States is eligible.



U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has informed some USRAP applicants in South Africa that their cases are… pic.twitter.com/OQoIe6g2KY — U.S. Mission SA (@USEmbassySA) October 25, 2026

The US Embassy emphasised that all refugees admitted to the United States must meet the necessary eligibility requirements and must pass security and medical screenings.



Applicants to the refugee programme must meet the following requirements:

Must be a South African national, living in South Africa

Belong to a racial minority in South Africa, for example, a white Afrikaner.

Must be able to explain a past experience of persecution or a fear of future persecution.

Must be at least 18, or be referred with a qualifying parent.

WHY ARE APPLICATIONS BEING DENIED?

According to authorities, refugee applications have been rejected, and some individuals have had their status revoked by USCIS based on the following reasons…

Fraud and misrepresentation

Ineligibility as per requirements

Security and terrorism concerns

Criminal history

The UCIS has stated that it is under no obligation to grant an appeal to a rejected refugee applicant.



However, in rare cases, the application may be reviewed if evidence is missing or a factual error is found. This is entirely discretionary.

BACKLASH FROM REJECTED APPLICANTS

The US Embassy’s statement has been met with scores of comments criticising the refugee programme and its growing rejection of applicants.

Here’s what a few had to say on X…

@FredAmerikaner: “The high rate of ineligibility decisions will be the death of the programme. Why risk it if it means you will be stuck here forever?”



@ShadowEchoX: “Hundreds of us were lied to and dragged along for almost a year, believing that today we would get our tickets. But all we got was a letter that crushed all hope and belief that we were saved”

@art03837827: “All bullsh*t. People who met all the criteria were rejected.”
