The strike came as a separate, US-brokered ceasefire in southern Ukraine was reported to be holding around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in the Kherson region. Ukrainian and Russian human rights ombudsmen said on Wednesday that the local truce had passed 30 hours without an incident. Images released by Russia's Defence Ministry purportedly show military engineers clearing mines near Oleshky, although the filming date was not provided.

The operation is intended to open routes for humanitarian aid and allow residents who wish to leave to do so. Around 2,000 people are believed to remain in the city, where food, water and medicine have been scarce for months. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed the respite but said the evacuation of civilians would be crucial to the truce's success.

World.title: Spain: minute of silence for train crash victims as king visits hospital
World.content:
Opposition People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo visited the scene, while King Felipe VI travelled to a hospital in Toledo treating survivors of the disaster. The monarch was greeted by hospital staff and other people waiting outside before entering the building.

 

Meanwhile, rescue teams continued searching the wreckage with sniffer dogs, as cranes lifted damaged carriages and emergency workers combed through debris scattered down a gravel embankment. One more body was recovered overnight, bringing the death toll to 69, according to Castilla-La Mancha regional president Emiliano García-Page, who said 50 people remained in hospital.

The collision occurred on Wednesday morning when a high-speed train operated by state-owned Renfe struck the rear of a stationary Iryo service in central Spain. At least three carriages were thrown down an embankment by the impact.

The government declared three days of national mourning from Thursday, as the country's second deadly high-speed rail disaster this year raised fresh questions about railway safety.

In January, 46 people were killed in another collision involving Renfe and Iryo trains on the same line. The latest crash, just four weeks before a national election, has also disrupted rail travel, with the high-speed route between Madrid and Seville closed and thousands of passengers seeking alternative transport.

World.title: The World Judo Tour returns to Abu Dhabi with Day 1 wins
World.content:
Fresh off the World Championships, the World Judo Tour returned to the Mubadala Arena for the prestigious Abu Dhabi Grand Slam.

 

In the -48kg final Turkiye’s Merve AZAK took on Azerbaijan’s Konul ALIYEVA.

ALIYEVA got the historic win, achieving the first ever women’s Grand Slam gold medal for Azerbaijan.

Mr Marius Vizer, President of the International Judo Federation, awarded the medals.

At -60kg top seed Azerbaijan's Balabay AGHAYEV. took on 18 year old Loiq KUDBUDINOV.

Showcasing why he was the favourite Aghayev showed speed and skill to score a dynamic ippon!

International Judo Federation Vice President Dr Laszlo TOTH awarded the medals.

It’s a wonderful place. I’ve been here before. I took a bronze medal here in the past, but no i’m happy to replace that bronze medal with gold! Balabay AGHAYEV (AZE)

In the -52kg final Olympic medalist Amandine BUCHARD took on Tihea TOPOLOVEC of Croatia.

TOPOLOVEC scored a clever waza ari to win her first ever Grand Slam gold medal!

IOC Member Mr Balazs FÜRJES awarded the medals.

I’ve been a few times in Abu Dhabi, this is my first time leaving with a medal, so now it will be one of my favourite cities. Tihea TOPOLOVEC (CRO)

At -66kg Bahrain’s Sukhrob BOQIEV’s first world tour final was against Iago ABULADZE.

Boqiev defied his world ranking of 277 to take a shock gold!

The medals were awarded by International Judo Federation Vice President Mr Obaid AL ANZI.

At -57kg Brazil’s Shirlen NASCIMENTO took on France’s Martha FAWAZ.

Two waza ari scores, the first an opportune o soto after a weak attack from Nascimento.

And the second, a driving o uchi gari that travelled across the mat, gave Fawaz a second grand slam title.

International Judo Federation Vice President Mr Siteny RANDRIANASOLONIAIKO awarded her the gold medal.

The home team also didn’t disappoint, with some top action from the UAE’s Narmandakh BAYANMUNKH.

Join us for day two of the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam tomorrow.

World.title: Actor Patrick Stewart, star of 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men', dies aged 86
World.content:
The legendary British actor Patrick Stewart has died. He was 86.

 

Best known to millions around the world for portraying Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films and Captain Jean-Luc Picard in the sci-fi television series Star Trek: The Next Generation and subsequent films, Stewart spent much of his early career on stage.

A post on the actor's official Instagram and X accounts said: "We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia."

"He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all."

A statement announcing the actor's death, on the official X account of the late Sir Patrick Stewart

A career spanning seven decades

Stewart's career on stage and screen spanned nearly seven decades. It began in Mirfield, northern England, before he trained as an actor and later joined the Royal Shakespeare Company.

His theatrical roles ranged from Claudius to Macbeth. He also frequently performed a one-man adaptation of A Christmas Carol and appeared alongside his longtime friend Ian McKellen in West End and Broadway productions of Harold Pinter's No Man's Land and Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot.

Stewart received numerous honours throughout his career, including a Grammy and two Laurence Olivier Awards, as well as Emmy, Golden Globe and Tony nominations. He was also honoured with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010.

As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Stewart appeared throughout the seven-season run of Star Trek: The Next Generation between 1987 and 1994. He also starred in four Star Trek films before returning to the role on the small screen in Star Trek: Picard from 2020 to 2023.

Patrick Stewart arrives at the premiere of the third and final season of "Star Trek: Picard". 9 Feb 2023 Richard Shotwell/Invision/AP, File

Tributes paid to the internationally acclaimed actor

In a post on Instagram, actor George Takei, who also starred in the Star Trek franchise, wrote: "As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, Patrick Stewart took the Starship Enterprise to places it had never gone before, and he inspired a whole next generation of star-gazers who looked longingly ahead to a brighter future for all humanity."

"Our hearts are heavy, indeed. Rest in the heavens, Captain."

Actor Hugh Jackman, who starred alongside Stewart in the X-Men films, described him as a "tremendous friend and man". In a post on Instagram, he wrote: "We lost one of the greats of stage and screen today."

"I learned so much from him. I will miss you, Patrick Stewart, all of my days."

Marvel Studios also paid tribute to Stewart, saying he brought Charles Xavier to life with "extraordinary grace, intelligence, and humanity, defining the character for generations of fans, from X-Men to Logan to Avengers: Doomsday."

Marvel Studios, which makes the 'Avengers' film franchise, paid tribute to Stewart in a post on X

The post continued: "He was a singular talent, a generous collaborator, and a true gentleman. Our hearts go out to his wife Sunny, his children, his friends, and the countless fans around the world whose lives he touched with his art."

William Shatner, who starred alongside Stewart in Star Trek Generations, also paid tribute to him on X. He wrote "Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work."

A tribute from Sir Patrick's Star Trek co-star, William Shatner, on X

The UK's Defence Secretary Wes Streeting also honoured Stewart. In a post on X, he wrote: "He never forgot his roots, nor did he shy away from using his voice to stand up for others, particularly those affected by domestic violence."

He was also a prominent campaigner against domestic violence, speaking publicly about his childhood experiences of witnessing his father abuse his mother and supporting organisations working with survivors.

Stewart is survived by his wife, Sunny Ozell, and his two adult children from his first marriage, Daniel and Sophie Stewart.

World.title: Germany and Ukraine test armed ground robot for frontline deployment
World.content:
A German and a Ukrainian defence company have tested an armed ground robot for use by Ukrainian forces, with the first systems due to be integrated and delivered by the end of 2026.

 

The cooperation agreement was signed in early October during German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's state visit to Kyiv, in the presence of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Before the end of 2026, the first robotic vehicles fitted with the new weapons modules are expected to be ready for deployment and delivered in line with the needs of Ukraine's armed forces.

How the new system works

It's known as GEREON. Built by ARX Robotics, the unmanned vehicle provides mobility and power and can carry out reconnaissance using cameras and sensors.

It can be fitted with the SABER weapons module, built by Ukrainian company ROBONEERS, which is mounted on top and provides remotely operated fire support for attack and defence capabilities. The companies say this allows soldiers to operate the system from a safer distance.

ARX ROBOTICS GEREON UGV with ROBONEERS SABER ARX Robotics

Unarmed versions of GEREON are already being used for a range of tasks in Ukraine. They can transport supplies, evacuate wounded personnel, support electronic warfare, carry out reconnaissance and counter drones. The platform can also be adapted for combat missions.

The companies say the aim is to create one flexible robotic system that can be quickly adapted for different frontline missions.

The SABER weapons module is also customisable, allowing soldiers to fit different weapons depending on the mission, from rifles to grenade launchers.

ARX says GEREON is the largest fleet of Western-built unmanned ground vehicles currently being used in Ukraine.

Maximilian Wied, CFO and co-founder of ARX Robotics, said: "Modern land forces need combat platforms that can be quickly adapted to different missions, integrate new technologies and work seamlessly with existing systems."

ROBONEERS says its robotic systems have already been used in more than 15,000 frontline missions since 2014.

The two companies are already cooperating in other areas. They have set up a joint venture to expand production of another unmanned ground vehicle, the Rys Pro, in Germany and Ukraine. The companies are targeting production of more than 1,000 units in its first year.

German defence minister to visit tech company Helsing

Artificial intelligence is also a focus for German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius, who is visiting defence technology company Helsing at its headquarters in Munich.

The visit will focus on the company's latest products and AI capabilities, alongside meetings with management, employees and the works council.

Helsing was founded in 2021 and has grown rapidly into one of Europe's most prominent defence technology companies.

It develops artificial intelligence and software for military systems, including technology designed to add AI capabilities to existing platforms such as tanks, submarines and fighter jets.

World.title: Kazakhstan's Tokayev calls for faster construction of nuclear power plants
World.content:
Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called for a long-term national uranium reserve and faster progress on building two nuclear power plants (NPPs) in his annual state-of-the-nation address on Wednesday.

 

“I believe it is possible, and perhaps even necessary, to begin construction of the Balkhash NPP as early as next year, and to sign a comprehensive cooperation agreement with the goal of launching construction of the Moyynkum NPP as soon as possible,” he said.

Tokayev highlighted that nuclear energy is one way to achieve an electricity surplus, which he described as essential for digitalising the economy and integrating artificial intelligence into all areas of public life.

He also criticised the government over inefficient energy management and corruption schemes in the sector. During winter shortages, Kazakhstan buys electricity from neighbouring countries at high prices, only to sell it back at much lower rates in summer.

“It’s a rather simple sort of ‘business’, and one that has persisted for decades. I’m assured that this is standard practice in the energy sector,” Tokayev said.

He added that such practices had also led to the deliberate obstruction of power plant construction and commissioning in several regions.

Logistics hub 'historic opportunity'

Tokayev opened his address by pointing to an increasingly unpredictable geopolitical environment, which he said “did not exist even during the Cold War."

Growing vulnerabilities along maritime routes, he argued, were increasing the importance of overland transport corridors.

“Kazakhstan must seize this historic opportunity to truly become a leading logistics hub for Eurasia,” he said.

The address came two months later than usual and was delivered at the parliament session. Press service of Kazakhstan President

He pointed to the construction of the Aral-Caspian Highway, which began in August. The project is expected to shorten the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route by 1,000 kilometres and reduce cargo delivery times to three days.

The Bakty–Ayagoz railway line is scheduled to launch next year. It will establish a third railway crossing with China and increase freight capacity by 20 million tonnes.

Tokayev said Kazakhstan needed to move beyond its role as a transit country and become an organiser of international freight flows.

He called for developing domestic logistics operators, creating distribution centres, and digitising the transport sector, while also instructing the government to focus on air transit and road infrastructure.

Address in numbers

According to the IMF's forecast, Kazakhstan's GDP will exceed €350 billion this year, making it the world's 47th-largest economy. GDP per capita is expected to surpass €17,000.

The industrial sector now accounts for more than 14% of GDP. Tokayev attributed the growth to efforts to diversify the economy.

Small and medium-sized businesses contribute 40% of GDP, while their share of fixed capital investment has approached 70%.

Infographics of Kazakhstan's GDP Galiya Khassenkhanova

Kazakhstan's gold and foreign exchange reserves, combined with the National Fund's assets, have exceeded €110 billion. Tokayev said the country should use these resources to modernise infrastructure and improve living conditions across its regions.

Domestic bank assets have surpassed €130 billion, while savings accounts have reached a record €94 billion. Around 78% of these savings are held in the national currency, which Tokayev cited as a sign of the tenge's growing value.

The president designated next year as the Year of Nationwide Construction, calling on parliament to prioritise building and modernising public infrastructure, including roads, airports, hospitals and cultural centres.

The regions plan to build around 70 medical facilities and 50 educational, sports and cultural facilities. The National Fund is expected to allocate approximately €12.8 billion for these and other infrastructure projects by the end of 2029. Nearly €3 billion of that amount is earmarked for social projects over the next four months.

Tokayev also highlighted the country's demographic profile, noting that Kazakhstan has around seven million children, accounting for 34% of the population. More than 237,000 children have special educational needs.

Tokayev said the sector grew nearly 6% last year, with total output reaching almost €30 billion.

The address followed Kazakhstan's Day of the Republic and came as the country prepares to mark the 35th anniversary of its independence.

World.title: Paris shooting suspect admits targeting Muslims and people of African origin
World.content:
The suspect in the shooting in Trappes and La Verrière, on the outskirts of Paris, has admitted specifically targeting people he perceived to be Muslim or of African or North African origin, anti-terrorism public prosecutor Olivier Christen announced on Thursday.

 

Known only as Kévin T., the 39-year-old is accused of killing one man and injuring seven other people during the attack, which was carried out both from a car and on foot on 23 October.

"He admitted having specifically targeted people who are of a Muslim or African, North African type," the prosecutor said at a press conference. The suspect is also said to have explained that he chose Trappes because he regarded it as "a hideout for Islamists".

An attack prepared over a long period

The prosecutor stressed what he described as the "very extensive preparation" of the attack.

During questioning, Kévin T. acknowledged premeditation and said he had fired "in bursts". Investigators established that from September he had bought several items intended to improve the effectiveness of his weapon, a Sten-type submachine gun dating from the Second World War. He had also bought a police armband and handcuffs.

On the day of the attack, the suspect drove between Trappes and La Verrière, shooting at several people. The man killed, Pengo Bossio Wangi, was 26 and originally from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Among the seven injured was an 11-year-old girl whose life is no longer in danger. As of Thursday, three victims remained in hospital, one of them in a life-threatening condition.

A search of the suspect's home in Plaisir, also on the outskirts of Paris, uncovered an arsenal that included magazines, two brass knuckles, a steel bayonet and a silencer. Investigators also found a Quran, a Bible and a copy of Adolf Hitler's "Mein Kampf".

Stickers bearing nationalist slogans were also discovered. Many bore the words "Long live France, RN, proud to be French", referring to the far-right National Rally party, while others carried phrases including "100% French, long live France" and "Support for the security forces". The suspect admitted having designed and ordered them online, while insisting that he was neither a member nor a supporter of any political party.

Despite these admissions, he denied intending to commit a terrorist act and considered his actions "legitimate", according to the prosecutor.

He also denied having intended to kill children, saying he may have misjudged the height of the 11-year-old victim. He nevertheless said he felt "no regret".

The suspect had reported psychological and psychiatric problems. However, according to the prosecutor, a medical examination found no acute psychiatric decompensation or signs of hallucinations or delusions that would justify compulsory hospitalisation.

The National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor's Office has opened a judicial investigation into murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist act, with an aggravating circumstance linked to the presumed origin or religion of the victims. Prosecutors have requested that the suspect be placed in pre-trial detention.

Emmanuel Macron meets residents at Trappes town hall on 23 October 2026 AP Photo

Emmanuel Macron points the finger at the far right

Appearing on the YouTube channel HugoDécrypte on Wednesday, President Emmanuel Macron denounced what he called "a racism of atmosphere" and "a disinhibition of violence".

Macron blamed far-right political movements for helping create that climate, citing National Rally and groups close to it.

The RN reacted sharply on Thursday on television channel TF1. Party MP Jean-Philippe Tanguy described the president's comments as "very problematic", accusing him of having allowed "hateful ideologies" to flourish during his time in office.

A national tribute to the victims

A national tribute will be paid to the victims of the attack. The announcement was made on Wednesday 28 October by the government, the day after a request at the National Assembly by the leader of the Green MPs, Cyrielle Chatelain.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will preside over the ceremony, minister responsible for combating discrimination Aurore Bergé told the Senate.

A date and location have not yet been announced.

World.title: EU peacekeeping helicopter crash in Bosnia kills at least four
World.content:
An Italian helicopter taking part in an EU peacekeeping operation has crashed near the town of Brčko in northern Bosnia and Herzegovina.

 

The European Union's EUFOR military mission confirmed the CH-47 Chinook helicopter had crashed on Thursday afternoon. A spokesman said four crew members had been killed and 11 were injured.

A spokesman for Brčko hospital, said three of the 15 crew members on board the helicopter were killed in the crash and a fourth died in hospital.

"Twelve people were brought to our hospital. Unfortunately, a fourth person died from his injuries in hospital," said the spokesman, Salih Ibrahimbegovic.

EUFOR also said no civilians had been injured and no civilian infrastructure, property or vehicles were damaged in the crash.

Reaction from Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy and Vice-President of the European Commission

The crash happened in Gorice, about 180 kilometres (110 miles) northeast of Sarajevo.

"As a result of this crash, a number of EUFOR personnel tragically lost their lives, and others were seriously injured," EUFOR said in a later statement.

Bosnia's Defence Ministry said "it is not possible to issue further statements, while awaiting more precise information, above all about the state of health of the personnel".

EUFOR has urged people not to spread unverified information or disinformation and to rely on official channels for updates on the incident.

Brčko district mayor Siniša Milić said three people had died and 12 had been injured, with one of those injured in a critical condition.

"All have been treated in a hospital in Brčko. Medical staff are on alert," he said.

Further details about those on board and the cause of the crash are expected to be released once the authorities have completed their investigation.

EUFOR’s roughly 1,200-strong mission has operated in Bosnia since 2004, when it took over from NATO. It works under a UN Security Council mandate to help maintain security and oversee the military provisions of the peace agreement that ended the 1992–95 war.

World.title: US judge narrows Macrons' defamation lawsuit against American podcaster
World.content:
A judge in the United States has ruled that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte ​could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of the American podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself.

Advertising Read more

The Macrons had filed a lawsuit in July 2025 against Owens and two companies, accusing her of helping fan online rumours about whether Brigitte is a transgender woman.

Owens, 37, an influencer with a large following on social media platforms, has claimed that Brigitte was a man.

Delaware Superior Court Judge Sheldon Rennie said in a ruling on Tuesday that Owens could not be held personally liable in the case.

But Rennie allowed the suit against two companies associated with her – Candace Owens LLC and GeorgeTom Inc – to continue.

Question of jurisdiction

Rennie said the Delaware court did not hold jurisdiction over Owens because her residence was in another state, Tennessee.

The ruling means that if the French first couple were to eventually win the case, Owens' personal assets would be shielded.

In their lawsuit, the Macrons said Owens ⁠touted ​false claims and conspiracy theories ​against them "to promote her independent platform, gain notoriety, and make money".

Rennie deferred judgment on Owens' motion to dismiss ‌the ⁠Macrons' litigation until he was briefed on how French defamation law and statutes of limitation intersect with US law.

"I am in the absolute best mood over this Macron dismissal," Owens said on X on Wednesday.

'Centuries of patriarchal history': why trans rumours are wielded against women

Damages to Brigitte Macron

Brigitte Macron, 73, has taken to the courts in France to combat claims she was born a man.

Two French YouTubers, Natacha Rey and Amandine Roy, were convicted in September 2024 of spreading false claims after they posted a video in December 2021 alleging that Brigitte Macron had once been a man named Jean-Michel Trogneux – who is actually her brother.

Rey and Roy were ordered to pay €8,000 in damages to Brigitte Macron and €5,000 to Jean-Michel Trogneux.

The defendants were also given a suspended fine of €500.

Did French media silence enable Brigitte Macron fake news story to go viral?

Brigitte Macron had filed a libel complaint against the two women after their claim went viral, triggering conspiracy theories notably among the far right.

Roy, an online fortune-teller, interviewed Rey, a self-described independent journalist, for four hours on her YouTube channel in December 2021.

The women discussed the unsubstantiated rumour that Brigitte Macron had undergone gender reassignment, with Rey claiming to have uncovered a “state lie” and “scam”.

The claim went viral just weeks before France's 2022 presidential election, spreading even to the US where Owen derided the first lady in a now deleted YouTube video.

World.title: Egypt's mahrganat music: from the streets to five-star hotels
World.content:
Born in Egypt’s working-class neighbourhoods, mahraganat music is loud and raw, and these days it is practically impossible to escape. But for the artists behind it, mahraganat is more than just party music: they see it as the latest chapter in Egypt’s rich musical history.

Advertising

In this third episode of the season, we travel to the Egyptian capital, Cairo, to discover the origins of a genre that has become the soundtrack to urban life, despite receiving no official airtime.

Mahraganat evolved from shaabi: music by the people, for the people. Although it rose to prominence during the revolution of 2011–12, it has since become less overtly political.

It remains the music of happiness, partying, joy, and celebration.

Its fast rhythms and loud beats may be a far cry from the golden age of Egyptian music, but mahraganat has been on the scene since the early 2000s and it isn’t going anywhere, any time soon.

We trace its origins and evolution as we speak to one of the godfathers of the movement, his musical partner and a specialist in the genre.

Mid-East Junction is produced by RFI's English-language service. This episode was mixed by Vincent Pora. Special thanks to Elisa Schouten for her contribution.

World.title: Binance crypto platform suspends trades amid suspected hack
World.content:
The platform suspended some trading while crypto companies froze billions in their respective currencies. The full extent of the possible hack was not yet clear.

The world's largest cryptocurrency platform, Binance, confirmed on Thursday that it was investigating a potential security breach.

"It does look like a hack on Binance," said former company chief Changpeng Zhao, who remains a major shareholder.

Some $3 billion (€2.7 billion) had been frozen in response to the suspected hack.

"Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," a company spokesperson said.

"Binance will cover all hacking losses," co-founder Yi He said, without providing more details about the incident.

Binance 'reviewing' possible hack

The extent of the possible security breach was not immediately disclosed. Binance did not say whether any cryptocurrency funds had been stolen.

"Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information," the company statement said.

How to avoid crypto losses To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The company, which is the world's largest platform in terms of daily crypto trading volume, suspended trading on certain products while the freezing came from cryptocurrency companies using the platform.

Tether froze around $1.6 billion in its USDT currency, according to CEO Paolo Ardoino, and Circle froze some $800 million-worth of USDC, boss Jeremy Allaire said.

Who is Binance ex-CEO Zhao?

The news of the possible hack sent Bitcoin's value tumbling by 3.2% on Thursday evening, dropping below $79,000.

Zhao, who founded the Binance platform in 2017, said "as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered."

He stepped down as CEO after pleading guilty in 2023. to failing to prevent money laundering on his platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.

Zhao and Binance have been key supporters of cryptocurrency ventures by US President Donald Trump and his family.

World.title: Israeli election: Netanyahu, main rival fall short of majority after all votes counted
World.content:
10/30/2026 October 30, 2026 Tricky task of forming a working coalition begins

Ahead of the election, two clear coalitions had formed. On the one side, the ruling coalition of right-wing, far-right and religious parties centered around Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party.

On the other side was the anti-Netanyahu bloc, made up of a coalition of right-wing, centrist and liberal parties whose unifying principle was to oust Netanyahu from power.

However, neither of these blocs was able to secure a majority of seats, meaning a simple path to forming a government is off the table.

The task of figuring out a new working coalition is now beginning, with the question of whether the two Arab-Israeli lists, which together secured an unprecedented 19 seats, may form part of a future government or at least provide some form of support.

Yair Golan, chairman of the left-liberal Democrats, said he had met with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Yair Lapid and Mansur Abbas, head of the Arab Ra'am party.

He has called for discussions with the Arab-led parties, saying after his meeting with Eisenkot that "the rescue of Israel is at stake," in a post on X.

It remains to be seen if the right-wing factions of Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc would ultimately entertain the possibility of working with the Arab-led parties.

Another option that has been aired is the possibility of a unity government including both Netanyahu and Eisenkot, but such a move may be similarly distasteful for moderate voters.

World.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
World.content:
Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

German tennis star Alexander Zverev is set to become the new world No. 1 in tennis, capping a successful year where he won two Grand Slams.

Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the top spot in the sport. Becker reached No.1 some 35 years ago.

Zverev replaces Italy's Jannik Sinner, who previously held the world's No. 1 spot.

Zverev got there by reaching the quarter-finals of the Erste Bank Open in Vienna this week.

He is also the second-oldest first-time No. 1 ranked player after Australian John Newcombe.

"(It is) very special. To have the feeling to be on the top of the world is amazing," Zverev said.

"It is different than winning a tournament or a title, but it's such a special feeling to know that the No. 1 is going to be next to your name when the new rankings come out."

Among German female tennis players, only Steffi Graf and Angelique Kerber have achieved this in the WTA rankings.

Zverev beat Ben Shelton to win the US Open in September Image: Robert Deutsch/IMAGN Images/REUTERS

Two Grand Slams in 2026

Zverev's career had been defined by getting close to Grand Slam titles but never quite reaching them, facing stiff competition from Sinner and Spanish talent Carlos Alcaraz.

The Hamburg-born also won a gold medal in the 2021 Olympics.

But his tennis career finally had its breakthrough this year, when he won the Grand Slam at both the French and US Opens.

Known for his consistency, he was just the ninth man to reach at least the semifinals at all four majors in the same season.
